I. בֶ֫טֶן‎ noun feminineNum 5:25 belly, body, womb (Arabic ) — ׳בּ‎ absolute Judg 13:7 +; בָּ֑טֶן‎ 13:5 +; construct בֶּטֶן‎ Psa 139:13 +; suffix בִּטְנִי‎ Job 3:10 +; בִּטְנְךָ‎ Deut 7:13 +; בִּטְנֵךְ‎ Gen 25:23; בִּטְנוֺ‎ Job 15:2 +, etc.; —

1. a. belly, abdomen, of man Judg 3:21-22, of woman Num 5:21-22, 27; as beautiful in form Cant 7:3; as seat of hunger Prov 13:25; as eating Ezek 3:3 (|| מֵעִים‎); compare Prov 18:20 (figurative); as seat of passion, avarice, etc. Job 20:20, 23; in figure of God's casting riches out of extortioner's belly 20:15 (|| וַיְקִאֶנּוּ‎), compare also Psa 17:14; figurative of innermost part of man = inmost soul Prov 18:8 = 26:22; 20:27, 30 (all ב ׳חַדְרֵי‎); as seat of intell. faculties (= English breast or bosom) 22:18 (compare מֵעִים‎ Psa 40:9) Job 15:2; 15:35; 32:18, בִּטְנִי רוּחַ‎ 15:19; as trembling at theophany Hab 3:16.

b. belly of hippopotamus Job 40:16.

c. שְׁאוֺל בֶּטֶן‎ Jonah 2:3 (Jonah's prayer: || יַמִּים בִּלְבַכ מְצוּלָה‎).

2 body, opposed to soul Psa 31:10 (opposed to נֶפֶשׁ‎), also 44:26 (opposed to id.; — on this compare ZimBp 71).

3 womb Gen 25:23-24, 38:27 (all J) Hosea 12:4; Job 10:19 (|| רֶחֶם‎ 10:18) Eccl 11:5; Job 31:15 עָשָׂ֑הוּ עשֵֹׁנִי בַבֶּטֶן הֲלֹא‎ did not he that made me in the womb make him (|| אֶחָד בָּרֶחֶם וַיְכֻנֶנּוּ‎); compare Psa 139:13 בְּבֶטֶן תְּסֻכֵּנִי‎, & Jer 1:5; especially ב ׳מְּרִי‎ i.e. offspring Gen 30:2 (E) Psa 127:3; Isa 13:18; Prov 31:2 בִּטְנִי בַּר‎ = my son (|| בְּרִי‎) compare בֶּןבִּֿטְנָהּ‎ Isa 49:15; of birth מִבֶּטֶן יָצָא‎ Job 1:21; 3:11; Eccl 5:14; בֶּטֶן‎ alone = birth Hosea 9:11 (|| הֵרָיוֺן לֵדָה,‎), compare Figurative הַקָּ֑רַח יָצָא מִי מִבֶּטֶן‎ Job 38:29 out of whose womb came the ice ? compare בִּטְנִי דַּלְתֵי סָגַר לֹא‎ 3:10 i.e. of my (mother's) womb; מִבֶּטֶן גָּחָה‎ take, draw out of the womb, subject ׳י‎ (i.e. cause to be born) Psa 22:10; בֶטֶן מְּרִי‎used also of father Micah 6:7, compare Psa 132:11 (David as ancestor of Messianic King); Job 19:17 בִטְנִי בְּנֵי‎ sons of my body, of doubtful interpretation, perhaps = sons of my (mother's) womb, compare 3:10 (Ges De), i.e. my brother or men of my clan RSK 33 f., others my sons (Ew), my grandsons (Di); also in addressing Israel As a whole (masculine suffix) Deut 7:13; 28:4, 11, 18, 53; 30:9, compare בִטְנָם מַחֲמַדֵּי‎ Hosea 9:16 beloved ones of their womb; מִןהַֿבֶּטֶן (מִבֶּטֶן)‎ = from birth Judg 13:5, 7; Psa 58:4; 71:6, compare also Isa 44:2, 24; 46:3 (|| רָחַ֑ם‎) 48:8; 49:1, 5; נִמִּי מִבֶּטֶן‎ id. Judg 16:17; Job 31:18; Psa 22:11 (|| רֶחֶם‎).

4 architectural word of some rounded projection connected with the two pillars Jachin & Boaz 1Kin 7:20 (Klo reads הבית‎).

חמור.def:
H2543. chamor

I. חֲמוֺר‎ noun [masculine] heap, absolute ׳ח‎ with dual חֲמֹרָתָ֑יִם‎ (Baer ׳חְִמֹרֹת‎), as if from חֲמֹרָה‎; — חֲמֹרָתָ֑יִם חֲמוֺר הַחֲמוֺר בִּלְחִי‎ Judg 15:16 with the ass's jawbone, a heap, two heaps, i.e. so many slain.

חֲמֹרֹתָ֑יִם‎ see I. חֲמוֺר‎. above

II. חֲמוֺר‎ noun masculineGen 45:23 (he)-ass (Late Hebrew id. (sometimes female, but this regularly חֲמוֺרָה‎); Aramaic הֲמָרָא‎ Arabic , Palmyrene חמרא‎ ReckendZMG 1888, 404; as imêru, SchrCot Gloss; — name from reddish colour) — absolute חֲמוֺר‎ 22:5 43t.; חֲמֹר‎ Exod 13:13; Deut 22:10; construct חֲמוֺר‎ Exod 23:5 4t.; הֲמֹר‎ Gen 49:14; suffix חֲמֹרְךָ‎ Deut 5:14; 28:31; חֲמֹרֶ֑ךָ‎ Exod 23:12; חֲמֹרוֺ‎ Gen 22:3 8t.; plural חֲמוֺרִים‎ Judg 19:10 9t.; חֲמֹרִים‎ Gen 12:16 16t.; suffix חֲמוֺרֵינוּ‎ Judg 19:19; חֲמֹרֵינוּ‎ Gen 43:18; חֲמוֺרֵיכֶם‎ 1Sam 8:16; חֲמֹרֵיהֶם‎ Gen 34:28 4t.; חֲמוֺרֵיהֶם‎ Josh 9:4; — ass (he-ass; אתון‎ = she-ass) found in all periods (collective only Gen 32:6; Isa 21:7); —

1 as (valuable) property, with oxen, sheep, camels, slaves, etc. Gen 12:16; 24:35; Genesis 30:48; 47:17; Exod 9:3 (all J) 20:17 (E), 21:33; 22:8 (twice in verse); 22:9; 23:4-5, 12; Num 16:15; Josh 6:21; 7:24 (all J E); note also Exod 13:13 = 34:20 (J E; firstlings belong to ׳י‎); Gen 36:24; Num 31:28, 30, 34, 39, 45 (all P); Deut 5:14, 18; 22:3-4, Judg 6:4; 1Sam 8:16; 12:3; 15:3; 22:19; 27:9; 1Chr 5:21; Ezra 2:67 = Neh 7:68 (Baer), Zech 14:15; collective Gen 32:5 (J; || שׁוֺר‎), שִׁפְחָה עֶבֶד, צאֹן,‎, but plural (similar ||) 34:28 (P), 47:17 (J); compare also ׳ח יְתוֺמִים‎ Job 24:3 the orphans' ass (|| אַלְמָנָה שׁוֺר‎); as knowing its master's crib Isa 1:3 (|| שׁוֺר‎); found in camp 2Kin 7:7, 10 (both || סוּסִים‎); as harnessed לַה ׳מֶתֶג‎ Prov 26:3 (|| סוּס‎).

2 used for riding :

a. by women Exod 4:20 (J), Josh 15:18 (JE) = Judg 1:14; 1Sam 25:20, 23, 42, compare 2Chr 28:15.

b. by men 2Sam 16:2; 17:23; 19:27; 1Kin 2:40; 13:13 (twice in verse); 13:23-24, 27, 28 (twice in verse); Isa 21:7; Zech 9:9.

c. חמורים צֶמֶד‎ a pair of asses 2Sam 16:1 (for burdens and for riding); for man and woman Judg 19:3, 10, 19, 21; carrying dead body 19:28, compare ׳ח‎ 1Kin 13:29.

3 beast of burden Gen 22:3, 5 (compare 22:6), 42:26-27, 45:23 (all E) 43:18, 24; 44:3, 13 (all J), Josh 9:4 (JE), 1Sam 25:18; 1 Chronicles 12:41; Neh 13:15(compare also ח ׳צֶמֶד‎ 2Sam 16:1 above); metaphor of Issachar ׳ח נָּ֑רֶם‎ Gen 49:14 (poem), an ass of (strong) bones. — ׳ח לֶחֶם‎ 1Sam 16:20 read probably חֲמִשָּׁה‎ five, or better עֲשָׂרָה‎ ten, see We Dr.

4 used in tillage Isa 32:20; not to be used in ploughing with an ox (שׁוֺר‎) Deut 22:10.

5 parts of body of ass mentioned are: ח ׳לְחִי‎ Judg 15:15-16, jawbone, Samson's weapon; ח ׳ראֹשׁ‎ 2Kin 6:25 eaten in famine; ה ׳בְּשַׂר‎ Ezek 23:20 Genital organ of ass (contemptuous simile)

6 ה ׳קְבוּרַת‎ Jer 22:19 burial of an ass, in figure of ignominious treatment of a corpse.

חמות.def:
H2545. chamoth

[חָמוֺת‎] noun feminine husband's mother (Late Hebrew חָמוֺת‎, Aramaic חֲמָתָא‎; Arabic husband's mother; Assyrian êmêtu, ZimBP 48; Ethiopic ) — only suffix חֲמוֺתֵךְ‎ Ruth 2:11; 3:17; חֲמוֺתָהּ‎ 1:14 7t.; חֲמֹתָהּ‎ Micah 7:6; — of Naomi Ruth 1:14; 2:11, 18, 19 (twice in verse); 2:23; 3:1, 6, 16, 17; בַּחֲמֹתָהּ כַּלָּה בְאִמָּ֔הּ קָמָ֫ה בַּת‎ Micah 7:6.

חמט.def:
H2546. chomet

חֹ֫מֶט‎ noun [masculine] a kind of lizard, only in list of unclean creeping animals Lev 11:30 ׃ וְהַתִּנְשָֽׁמֶת וְהַחֹמֶט וְהַלְּטָאָ֑ה וְהַכֹּחַ וְהָאֲנָקָה‎ (Aramaic is chameleon).

חמטה.def:
H2547. Chumtah

חֻמְטָה‎ proper name, of a location city in Judah Josh 15:54, ᵐ5‎ Εὐμα, ᵐ5‎L Αμματα; site unknown.

חֲמִיטַל‎ see חמוטל‎ above

חמיץ.def:
H2548. chamits

חָמִיץ‎ adjective seasoned (namely with salt, or a salt herb — Arabic , Punic Ἀμουτ [ = ֗֗֗ חמוץ‎] DlauZMG 1873, 522; see Thes — rendering it more tasty), of provender for cattle יאֹכֵ֑לוּ חָמִיץ בְּלִיל‎ Isa 30:24.

חֻמְצָה‎ see I. חמץ‎ Infinitive

חמישי.def:
H2549. chamishi

חֲמִישִׁי‎ masculine, חֲמִישִׁית‎

feminine adjective ordinal number fifth; — masculine חֲמִישִׁי‎ Gen 1:23 22t.; חֲמִשִׁי‎ Zech 7:3 3t.; feminine חֲמִישִׁית‎ absolute 1Kin 14:25 4t.; חֲמִשִׁית‎ Lev 19:25; Jer 36:9; חֲמִשּׁית‎ 1Kin 6:31; construct חֲמִישִׁית‎ Lev 27:15, 19; suffix חֲמִישִׁתוֺ‎ 5:16 2t.; חֲמִשִׁיתוֺ‎ 22:14; 27:31; חֲמִשִׁתוֺ‎ 27:27, compare חֲמִשִׁתָיו‎ Leviticus 5:24, read תוֺ‎- Samaritan Di (q. v.); — fifth, usually in enumerated days, months, years, sons, etc.; definite, except masculine Gen 1:23; 30:17, feminine 47:24; 1Kin 6:31; Neh 6:5; —

1. masculine Gen 1:23; Num 7:36; 29:26; 33:38; Josh 19:24 (all P), Gen 30:17 (E), Judg 19:8; 2Kin 25:8; Jer 1:3; 28:1; 52:12; Zech 7:3; 1Chr 27:8; Ezra 7:8-9, noun omitted 2Sam 3:4; 1Chr 2:14; 3:3; 8:2; 26:3-4, (all of בֵּן‎), 24:9; 25:12 (גּוֺרָל‎), Zech 8:19 (חֹדֶשׁ‎), 1Chr 27:8 (יוֺם‎).

2. feminine Lev 19:25; 1Kin 14:25; Jer 36:9; Ezek 1:2; 2Chr 12:2; ח ׳מַּעַם‎ Neh 6:5.

3 חֲמִשִּׁית‎ 1Kin 6:31 as substantive a fifth part, so חֲמִישִׁית‎ Gen 47:24; Lev 5:6; Leviticus 5:24; 22:14; 27:13, 27, 31; Num 5:7; construct כֶּסֶף חמישׁית‎ Lev 27:15, 19.

III. חמשׁ‎ (√ of following; meaning dubious).

חמישית.def:
H2549. chamishi

חֲמִישִׁי‎ masculine, חֲמִישִׁית‎

feminine adjective ordinal number fifth; — masculine חֲמִישִׁי‎ Gen 1:23 22t.; חֲמִשִׁי‎ Zech 7:3 3t.; feminine חֲמִישִׁית‎ absolute 1Kin 14:25 4t.; חֲמִשִׁית‎ Lev 19:25; Jer 36:9; חֲמִשּׁית‎ 1Kin 6:31; construct חֲמִישִׁית‎ Lev 27:15, 19; suffix חֲמִישִׁתוֺ‎ 5:16 2t.; חֲמִשִׁיתוֺ‎ 22:14; 27:31; חֲמִשִׁתוֺ‎ 27:27, compare חֲמִשִׁתָיו‎ Leviticus 5:24, read תוֺ‎- Samaritan Di (q. v.); — fifth, usually in enumerated days, months, years, sons, etc.; definite, except masculine Gen 1:23; 30:17, feminine 47:24; 1Kin 6:31; Neh 6:5; —

1. masculine Gen 1:23; Num 7:36; 29:26; 33:38; Josh 19:24 (all P), Gen 30:17 (E), Judg 19:8; 2Kin 25:8; Jer 1:3; 28:1; 52:12; Zech 7:3; 1Chr 27:8; Ezra 7:8-9, noun omitted 2Sam 3:4; 1Chr 2:14; 3:3; 8:2; 26:3-4, (all of בֵּן‎), 24:9; 25:12 (גּוֺרָל‎), Zech 8:19 (חֹדֶשׁ‎), 1Chr 27:8 (יוֺם‎).

2. feminine Lev 19:25; 1Kin 14:25; Jer 36:9; Ezek 1:2; 2Chr 12:2; ח ׳מַּעַם‎ Neh 6:5.

3 חֲמִשִּׁית‎ 1Kin 6:31 as substantive a fifth part, so חֲמִישִׁית‎ Gen 47:24; Lev 5:6; Leviticus 5:24; 22:14; 27:13, 27, 31; Num 5:7; construct כֶּסֶף חמישׁית‎ Lev 27:15, 19.

III. חמשׁ‎ (√ of following; meaning dubious).

חמל.def:
H2550. chamal

חָמַל‎ verb spare (Arabic ; is bear, become responsible; Aramaic comportavit, congessit); —

Qal Perfect ׳ח‎ 1Sam 15:15 3t.; חָמָ֑ל‎ 2Sam 12:6; Lam 2:17; חָמָ֑לְתָּ‎ 2:21; 3:43; וְחָמַלְתִּ֫י‎ Mal 3:17; Imperfect יַחְמֹל‎ Job 16:13 6t.; יַחְמוֺל‎ 6:10 3t.; וַיַּחְמֹל‎ 1Sam 15:9 3t.; 3 feminine singular וַתַּחְמֹל‎ Exod 2:6; 2masculine singular תַּחְמֹל‎ Deut 13:9; 1Sam 15:3; אֶחְמֹל‎ Ezek 8:18; 9:10; אֶחְמוֺל‎ Jer 13:14 4t.; וָאֶחְמֹל‎ Ezek 36:21; יַחְמֹ֑לוּ‎ Isa 9:18; תַּחְמְלוּ‎ Jer 50:14; 51:3; תַּחְמֹ֑לוּ‎ Ezek 9:5; Infinitive construct חֻמְלָה‎ 16:5 (Ges§ 45, 1. b); — spare, have compassion, with על‎ Exod 2:6 (E), 1Sam 15:3, 9, 15; 23:21; 2Sam 21:7; 2Chr 36:15, 17; Jer 15:5; Ezek 16:5; 36:21; Job 20:13; Zech 11:5-6, Mal 3:17 (twice in verse); Joel 2:18; Deut 13:9 (|| חוס‎ followed by על‎), Jer 21:7 (|| חוס‎ followed by על‎ + רחם‎), Ezek 9:10 (|| חוס‎ followed by על‎according to ᵑ7 ᵑ6‎ Co); followed by אֶלֿ‎ Jer 51:3; Isa 9:18; note poetic ׳אַלתַּֿחְ אֶלחֵֿץ‎ = spare no arrow Jer 50:14; followed by Infinitive 2Sam 12:4; absolute 12:6; Isa 30:14; Lam 2:17, 21, also 2:2 where apparently followed by accusative, 3:43; Job 6:10; 16:13; 27:22; Prov 6:34; Hab 1:17; || חוס‎ Ezek 5:11; 7:4 (strike out Co as doubl. of 7:9), 7:9; 8:18; 9:5; Jer 13:14 (|| אחוס‎ and ארחם‎).

חמלה.def:
H2550. chamal

חָמַל‎ verb spare (Arabic ; is bear, become responsible; Aramaic comportavit, congessit); —

Qal Perfect ׳ח‎ 1Sam 15:15 3t.; חָמָ֑ל‎ 2Sam 12:6; Lam 2:17; חָמָ֑לְתָּ‎ 2:21; 3:43; וְחָמַלְתִּ֫י‎ Mal 3:17; Imperfect יַחְמֹל‎ Job 16:13 6t.; יַחְמוֺל‎ 6:10 3t.; וַיַּחְמֹל‎ 1Sam 15:9 3t.; 3 feminine singular וַתַּחְמֹל‎ Exod 2:6; 2masculine singular תַּחְמֹל‎ Deut 13:9; 1Sam 15:3; אֶחְמֹל‎ Ezek 8:18; 9:10; אֶחְמוֺל‎ Jer 13:14 4t.; וָאֶחְמֹל‎ Ezek 36:21; יַחְמֹ֑לוּ‎ Isa 9:18; תַּחְמְלוּ‎ Jer 50:14; 51:3; תַּחְמֹ֑לוּ‎ Ezek 9:5; Infinitive construct חֻמְלָה‎ 16:5 (Ges§ 45, 1. b); — spare, have compassion, with על‎ Exod 2:6 (E), 1Sam 15:3, 9, 15; 23:21; 2Sam 21:7; 2Chr 36:15, 17; Jer 15:5; Ezek 16:5; 36:21; Job 20:13; Zech 11:5-6, Mal 3:17 (twice in verse); Joel 2:18; Deut 13:9 (|| חוס‎ followed by על‎), Jer 21:7 (|| חוס‎ followed by על‎ + רחם‎), Ezek 9:10 (|| חוס‎ followed by על‎according to ᵑ7 ᵑ6‎ Co); followed by אֶלֿ‎ Jer 51:3; Isa 9:18; note poetic ׳אַלתַּֿחְ אֶלחֵֿץ‎ = spare no arrow Jer 50:14; followed by Infinitive 2Sam 12:4; absolute 12:6; Isa 30:14; Lam 2:17, 21, also 2:2 where apparently followed by accusative, 3:43; Job 6:10; 16:13; 27:22; Prov 6:34; Hab 1:17; || חוס‎ Ezek 5:11; 7:4 (strike out Co as doubl. of 7:9), 7:9; 8:18; 9:5; Jer 13:14 (|| אחוס‎ and ארחם‎).

חמם.def:
H2527. chom

חֹם‎ noun masculineJer 17:8 heat; — חֹם‎ absolute Gen 8:22 3t. + 1Sam 21:7 (see below); construct Gen 18:1+ 3t.; of heat of (mid-) day היום חֹם‎ 18:1 (J), 1Sam 11:11; 2Sam 4:5; in promise of regular seasons Gen 8:22 (opposed to קֹר‎); compare Isa 18:4 (twice in verse) (׳ח קָצִיר‎); but as dangerous to plant-life Jer 17:8; it melts snow Job 24:19; חֹם לֶחֶם‎ 1Sam 21:7 bread of heat = hot bread, read perhaps ׳ל חָם‎ (as Josh 9:12).

חמן.def:
H2553. chamman

[חַמָּן‎] noun masculine sun-pillar, used in idolatrous worship (see Thes489ff. RSSemitic i, 469, LagM i, 228 Now Archaeology ii, 302; = Palmyrene חמנא‎ VogNo. 123 a; **+?N. Semitic Inscr., No. 136; LzbEphem. ii {1906}, 280; Phoenician חמן לבעל‎ often as epithet of solar Baal); — only plural absolute חַמָּנִים‎ Isa 27:9 4t.; suffix חַמָּנֵיכֶם‎ Lev 26:30 2t.; || בָּמוֺת‎ 26:30 (H), 2Chr 14:4, compare Ezek 6:4, 6; || הבעלים מזבחות‎2Chr 34:4; || אשׁרים‎ Isa 17:8; 27:9; || אשׁרים‎ and מְּסִלִים‎2Chr 34:7.

חמס.def:
H2554. chamas

[חָמַס‎] verb treat violently, wrong (Late Hebrew id., act violently, treat violently; Aramaic חֲמַס‎ (rare) violently seize; Arabic is be hard, strict, rigorous) —

Qal Perfect3plural חָֽמְסוּ‎ Ezek 22:26; Zeph 3:4; Imperfect יַחְמֹס‎ Job 15:33, וַיַּחְמֹס‎ Lam 2:6; תַּחְמֹ֑סוּ‎ Job 21:27; Jer 22:3; Participle חֹמֵס‎ Prov 8:36; — treat violently, wrong; —

1 of physical wrong: ׳תַּחְ‎ Jer 22:3 (|| תֹּנוּ‎) of wrong to widows and orphans; ׳וַיַּח שֻׂכּוֺ כַּגַּן‎ Lam 2:6 and hath done violence to his pavilion as to a garden (|| מֹעֲדוֺ שִׁחֵת‎); so, figurative, of vine, wrong, i.e. fail to nourish, kill בִּסְרוֺ ׳יַח כַּגֶּפֶן‎ Job 15:33.

2 of ethical wrong, object תּוֺרָה‎ Zeph 3:4; Exod 22:26 (both || קֹדֶשׁ חִלֵּל‎); compare תַּחְמֹ֑סוּ עָלֵי מְזִמּוֺת‎ Job 21:27 the devices (wherewith) ye do me violence.

3 both physical and ethical נַפְשׁוֺ חֹמֵס חֹטְאִי‎ Prov 8:36.

Niph`al Perfect3plural נֶחְמְסוּ‎ Jer 13:22 thy heels suffer violence (|| שׁוּלַיִךְ נִגְלוּ‎).

חמץ.def:
H2558. chomets

חֹ֫מֶץ‎ noun masculine vinegar — ׳ח‎ absolute Prov 10:26 3t.; construct Num 6:3 (twice in verse); — a common condiment Ruth 2:14, forbidden to Nazirite (׳ח יין‎ and ׳ח שֵׁכָר‎) Num 6:3 (twice in verse) (P), offered (in cruelty) to a thirsty man Psa 69:22 (figurative for harshness lack of sympathy); in simile of sluggard לַשִּׁנַּיִם כַּחֹמֶץ‎ Prov 10:26, ׳ח עַלנָֿ֑תֶר‎ 25:20 vinegar on nitre (simile of merry songs for the heavy-hearted).

חמק.def:
H2559. chamaq

חָמַק‎ verb turn away (intransitive) —

Qal Perfect3masculine singular ח ׳וְדוֺדִי עָבָ֑ר‎ Song 5:6 and my beloved had turned away, passed on.

Hithpa`el Imperfect2feminine singular הַשּׁוֺבֵבָה הַבַּת תִּתְחַמָּקִין עַדמָֿתַי‎ Jer 31:22 turn hither and thither, see Gf VB.

חמר.def:
H2561. chemer

חֶ֫מֶר‎ noun [masculine] wine (poetry) (Aramaic חַמְרָא‎; Arabic , see LagBN 207) — וְדַםעֵֿנָבתִּשְׁתֶּהחָֿ֑מֶר‎ Deut 32:14; חֶמֶר כֶּרֶם‎ Isa 27:2, but read here חֶמֶד כֶּרֶם‎ (see חֶמֶד‎).

חֲמַר‎ noun masculine wine (ᵑ7‎ Syriac; Biblical Hebrew חֶמֶר‎ (in poetry and late), √ I. חמר‎); — absolute ׳ח‎ Ezra 6:9; 7:22; emphatic חַמָרָא‎ Dan 5:1.5:2. 5:4. 5:23.

חמרן.def:
H2566. Chamran

חַמְרָן‎ proper name, masculine 1Chr 1:41 ( = חֶמְדָּן‎ Gen 36:26 q. v.)

חמש.def:
H2569. chomesh

I. חֹ֫מֶשׁ‎ noun [masculine] fifth part — only לַהֹמֶשׁ לְפַרְעֹה‎ Gen 47:26, but connection with preceding awk-ward; read perhaps הַחֹמֶשׁ‎ (ᵑ6‎), or ᵐ5 לְחַמֵּשׁ‎, see Di.

חמת.def:
H2575. Chammath

I. חַמַּת‎ proper name, of a location (hot spring) — town in Naphtali Josh 19:35 (perhaps = חַמּוֺן‎

2 see Di); ᵐ5‎ Ωμαθαδακεθ (= רַקַּת חַמַּת‎), A Αμαθ, ᵐ5‎L Αμμαθ; JosAnt. xviii, 2. 3 Αμμαθους (ed. Niese), compare Id.BJ. iv, 10.3GutheZPV 1891, xiii, 284; probably = Talmud „amata NbrGéogr. du Talm. 207 (with hot springs), 35 minutes south of Tiberias, see RobBR ii, 385 BuhlZPV xiii, 1890, 39 f. Guthel. with GASmGeogr, 450 (FurrerZPV ii, 1878, 55; xiii, 1890, 194 ff. and others say north of Tiberias); see חַמּוֺן דּאֹר, חַמֹּת‎ below & above

II. חַמַּת‎ proper name, masculine father of the house of Rechab 1Chr 2:55.

חַמַּת‎ proper name, of a location see below חמם‎.

חַנָּה חֵנָדָד, חֵן,‎ see below חנן‎.

חמת דאר.def:
H2576. Chammoth

Dor דּאֹר חַמֹּת‎ proper name, of a location in Naphtali, Levitical city Josh 21:32 (perhaps = 1. חַמּוֺן חַמַּת,‎

2 see Di), ᵐ5‎ Νεμμαθ, A Εμαθδωρ, ᵐ5‎L Αμαθδωρ.

חמת צובא.def:
H2578. Chamath

Tsobah צוֺבָה צוֺבָא,‎ proper name, of a territory Σουβα, rarely Σωβα(λ): an Aramaean kingdom, time of (Saul and) David צוֺבָא אֲרַם‎ 2Sam 10:6, 8 (elsewhere צוֺבָה‎), צוֺבָה אֲרַם‎ Psa 60:2 (title); צ מֶלֶךְ ׳הֲדַדְעֶזֶר‎ 2Sam 8:3, 5, 12 = 1Chr 18:3, 5; 1Kin 11:23; 1Chr 18:9; ׳צ‎ also 19:6; צ ׳חֲמַת‎2Chr 8:3; original home of one of David's heroes 2Sam 23:36 (perhaps read also for proper name, masculine מִבְחָר‎ || 1Chr 11:38, compare Dr); צ ׳מַלְכֵי‎ 1Sam 14:47 (only here in Saul's time); NöARAM, in Ency. Bib., compare ZMG xxv (1871), 113 ff. places between Hamath and Demascus (about „ums, Emesa), and so DlPa 279 f., who compare Assyrian city ‚ubitu, compare SchrCOT. 2Sam 8:8.

חמתי.def:
H2577. Chamathi

חֲמָתִי‎ adjective, of a people with article = substantive הַהֲמָתִ֑י‎, as descendants of Canaan Gen 10:18 = 1Chr 1:16.

חן.def:
H2580. chen

I. חֵן‎ noun masculinePsa 45:3 favour, grace; — ׳ח‎ Gen 6:8 67t.; suffix חִנּוֺ‎ 39:21; —

1 favour, grace, elegance:

a. of form and appearance, of a woman || יֹ֑פִי‎ Prov 31:30; חֵן אֵשֶׁת‎ 11:16; חן טובת זונה‎ Nahum 3:4; of a doe Prov 5:19; precious stone חן אבן‎ 17:8; of ornaments 1:9 = 4:9; 3:22.

b. of speech, lips Psa 45:3; Prov 22:11; words Eccl 10:12.

2 favour, acceptance:

a. with men Prov 13:15; 22:1; Eccl 9:11.

b. with God Zech 4:7 (twice in verse); 12:10; chiefly in phrases: בעיני חן מצא‎ find favour in the eyes of: (I) men Gen 30:27; 32:6; 33:8, 10, 15; 34:11; 39:4; 47:25, 29; 50:4; Num 32:5 (all J); Deut 24:1; Ruth 2:2, 10, 13; 1Sam 1:18; 16:22; 20:3, 29; 25:8; 27:5; 2Sam 14:22; 16:4; 1Kin 11:19; Est 5:8; 7:3; (2) of God Gen 6:8; 18:3; 19:19; Exod 33:12-13, (twice in verse); 33:16-17, 34:9; Num 11:11, 15 (all J); Judg 6:17; 2Sam 15:25; Prov 3:4; absolute חן מצא‎ (with man) 28:23; (with God) Jer 31:2; לפניו חן מֹצא‎ Est 8:5 (i.e. of the king); בעיני חן נתן‎ give favour in the eyes of (I) man Gen 39:21; Exod 3:21; 11:3; 12:36 (J); absolute חן נתן‎ of man Psa 84:12; (2) of God Prov 3:34; בְּעֵינֵי חֵן נשׂא‎ obtain favour in the eyes of Est 2:15; of the king 5:2; so לְפָנָיו וָחֶסֶד וַתִּשָּׂאחֵֿן‎ 2:17.

חנדד.def:
H2582. Chenadad

חֵנָדָד‎ proper name, masculine (חֵן‎ + הָדָד‎ favour of Hadad) — Levite chief Ezra 3:9; Neh 3:18, 24; 10:10.

חנה.def:
H2584. Channah

חַנָּה‎ proper name, feminine ᵐ5‎ Ἄννα (compare Nabataean חנה‎ EutNo. 20), mother of Samuel 1Sam 1:2 (twice in verse); 1:5 (twice in verse); 1:8-9, 13, 15, 19, 20, 22; 2:1, 21.

חנוך.def:
H2585. Chanok

חֲנוֺךְ‎ proper name, masculine 1. son of Cain Gen 4:17 (twice in verse); 4:18 ᵐ5‎ Ενωχ, ᵐ5‎L Ενως.

2 son of Jered (line of Seth), the pious Enoch, who walked with God and was taken by him Gen 5:18-19, 21, 22, 23, 24; 1Chr 1:3 ᵐ5‎ Ενωχ.

3 חֲנֹךְ‎ a son of Midian Gen 25:4; 1Chr 1:33, ᵐ5‎ Ενωχ.

4 חֲנוֺךְ‎ a son of Reuben Gen 46:9; Exod 6:14; Num 26:5; 1Chr 5:3, ᵐ5‎ Ενωχ.

חנון.def:
H2586. Chanun

חָנוּן‎ (favoured; compare Assyrian –anunu, king of Gaza COT on 2Kin 15:29); —

1 an Ammonite king 2Sam 10:1-2, 3, 4; 1Chr 19:2 (twice in verse); 19:3-4, 6.

2 Jewish chiefs, contemporaries of Nehemiah:

a. Neh 3:18.

b. Neh 3:30.

חנות.def:
H2588. chanuth

[חָנוּת‎] noun feminine cell (as having curved or vaulted roof, arched; see Thes Gf, and compare Aramaic vaulted room) — הַחֲנֻיּוֺת‎ Jer 37:16 (|| הַבּוֺר בֵּית‎).

חנט.def:
H2590. chanat

חָנַט‎ verb spice, make spicy, embalm (Late Hebrew id., bud, blossom; Arabic become mature, II. prepare for burial, spices for a corpse; embalmer, Dozyi, 322 after PS1320; Aramaic , חֲנַט‎ embalm; so Ethiopic (loan-word Di110)); —

Qal Perfect3feminine singular חָֽנְטָה‎ Song 2:13; Imperfect3masculine plural וַיַּחַנְטוּ‎ Gen 50:2, 26; Infinitive construct לַחֲנֹט‎ 50:2; —

1 spice, make spicy ח ׳הַתְּאֵנָה פַגֶּיהָ‎ Song 2:13 the fig-tree spiceth its figs, so VB De in translation (Ew De in notes Öttli and others prefer reddeneth, on account of spring season, compare the less common and perhaps secondary sense in Arabic become red (of leather) Lane657a).

2 embalm, followed by accusative of person Gen 50:2 (twice in verse) (performed by הָרֹפְאִים‎), 50:26.

חֲנֻטִים‎ noun [masculine] plural abstract embalming, only הַח ׳יְמֵי‎ Gen 50:3 i.e. the days consumed in the embalming process = יוֺם אַרְבָּעִים‎ see Di.

חנטים.def:
H2590. chanat

חָנַט‎ verb spice, make spicy, embalm (Late Hebrew id., bud, blossom; Arabic become mature, II. prepare for burial, spices for a corpse; embalmer, Dozyi, 322 after PS1320; Aramaic , חֲנַט‎ embalm; so Ethiopic (loan-word Di110)); —

Qal Perfect3feminine singular חָֽנְטָה‎ Song 2:13; Imperfect3masculine plural וַיַּחַנְטוּ‎ Gen 50:2, 26; Infinitive construct לַחֲנֹט‎ 50:2; —

1 spice, make spicy ח ׳הַתְּאֵנָה פַגֶּיהָ‎ Song 2:13 the fig-tree spiceth its figs, so VB De in translation (Ew De in notes Öttli and others prefer reddeneth, on account of spring season, compare the less common and perhaps secondary sense in Arabic become red (of leather) Lane657a).

2 embalm, followed by accusative of person Gen 50:2 (twice in verse) (performed by הָרֹפְאִים‎), 50:26.

חֲנֻטִים‎ noun [masculine] plural abstract embalming, only הַח ׳יְמֵי‎ Gen 50:3 i.e. the days consumed in the embalming process = יוֺם אַרְבָּעִים‎ see Di.

חניאל.def:
H2592. Channiel

חַנִּיאֵל‎ proper name, and חֲנִינָה‎ see below חנן‎

חֲנִית‎ see below חנה‎

I. חנך‎ (√ of following (see Arabic, Syriac); meaning unknown).

חַנִּיאֵל‎ proper name, masculine (favour of El; compare Phoenician חנמלקרת חנבעל,‎ (Hamilcar) favour of Melqart Nabataean חנאל‎ VogNo. 10) —

1 prince of tribe of Manasseh Num 34:23.

2 a chief of the tribe of Asher 1 Chronicles 7:89.

חניך.def:
H2593. chanik

[חָנִיךְ‎] adjective trained, tried, experienced, only plural suffix בֵיתוֺ יְלידֵי חֲנִיכָיו‎, Gen 14:14 i.e. his tried and trusty men, born in his house.

חנינה.def:
H2594. chaninah

חֲנִינָה‎ noun feminine favour חֲנִינָה לָכֶם לֹאאֶֿתֵּן‎ I will shew you no favour Jer 16:13 (see on form BaNB 136).

חנית.def:
H2595. chanith

חֲנִית‎ noun feminine spear (as flexible? see Thes); — absolute חֲנִית‎ 2Sam 13:19 26t.; construct id. 1Sam 26:16 (so 26:22 Qr, where Kt has article); suffix חֲנִיתָ֑ךָ‎ Hab 3:11; חֲנִיתוֺ‎ 1Sam 17:7 (twice in verse) + 11 t. + 2Sam 23:8, see below; plural חֲנִיתִים‎2Chr 23:9; חֲנִיתוֺתֵיהֶם‎ Isa 2:4 = חֲנִיתֹתֵיהֶם‎ Micah 4:3; —

1 spear, as hurled 1Sam 18:10-11, 19:9-10, (twice in verse); 20:33; held by king 22:6; sign of king's presence 26:7-8, 11, 12, 16, 22 (see RSK 171); also 2Sam 1:6; 2:23; 21:19; 23:18, 21 (3 t. in verse); 1Chr 11:11 = 2Sam 23:8, where read אֶתחֲֿנִיתוֺ עוֺרֵר הוּא‎ (for הָעֶצְנִו֯ עֲדִינוֺ הוּא‎) according to Ew Th Ke Klo Dr (not We), 1Chr 11:20, 23 (3 t. in verse); plural 2Chr 23:9; often || חֶרֶב‎ 1Sam 13:19, 22; 17:45, 47; 21:9; Isa 2:4 = Micah 4:3; Nahum 3:3; || שְׁלָטִים‎ 2Kin 11:10; || צִנָּה‎ 1Chr 12:35 (Baer); מַסָּע‎ Job 41:18; סְגֹד‎ Psa 35:3; || קֶשֶׁת‎ 46:10.

2. a. shaft of spear is ח ׳עֵץ‎ 2Sam 23:7; 1Chr 20:5 + 1Sam 17:7 Qr (doubtless right; Kt חץ‎).

b. spear-head ח ׳לַהֶבֶת‎ 1Sam 17:7, compare ח ׳לַהַב‎ Job 39:23; ח ׳בְּרַק‎ Nahum 3:3; Hab 3:11.

c. butt of spear ח ׳אַחֲרֵי‎ 2Sam 2:23.

3 metaphor of teeth of lions Psalm 2Sam 57:5 (|| חצים‎; figurative of Psalmist's enemies).

חנך.def:
H2596. chanak

II. חִָנִךְ‎ verb train up, dedicate (compare Arabic apparently denominative from rub palate of child with chewed dates, Lane659a, of midwife rub palate of new-born child with oil, etc., before it begins to suck, Dozyii, 332; also make experienced, submissive, etc. (as one does a horse by a rope in its mouth) Lane; see also WeSkizzen iii, 154; Late Hebrew חִנֵּךְ‎ accustom; Aramaic חֲנַךְ‎ dedicate, חַנֵּיךְ‎ as Late Hebrew; Ethiopic II. perceive, understand (Di108, initiatio is loan-word Id.ib.)) —

Qal Perfect3masculine singular suffix חֲנָכוֺ‎ Deut 20:5; Imperfect3masculine singular suffix יַחְנְכֶנּוּ‎ 20:5, 3masculine plural וַיַּחְנְכוּ‎ 1Kin 8:63; 2Chr 7:5; Imperative חֲנֹךְ‎ Prov 22:6; —

1 train, train up a (the) youth (לַנַּעַר‎) Prov 22:6 (compare Late Hebrew חִנּוּךְ‎).

2 dedicate, of formal opening of a new house Deut 20:5 (twice in verse); dedicate, consecrate temple 1Kin 8:63 2Chr 7:5 (all followed by accusative)

חנכה.def:
H2598. chanukkah

חֲנֻכָּה‎ noun feminine dedication, consecration, as a matter of usage only P and late (Late Hebrew חֲנוּכָּה‎ Feast of Dedication; so Aramaic חֲנוּכְּתָא‎) — abs ׳ח‎ Neh 12:27; construct חֲנֻכַּת‎ Num 7:10 6t.; dedication of wall of Jerusalem Neh 12:27 (twice in verse), by sacrifices and processions, with music; of altar in temple 2Chr 7:9; of 'the house' Psa 30:1 (title), i.e. the temple (re-dedication by Judas Maccabaeus, 1Macc 4:52ff.), see Ol Bae and others (opposed to De), and especially CheOP 234. 247; = dedication-offering for altar in tabernacle Num 7:10 (accusative with וַיַּקְרִיבוּ‎), compare הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לַחֲנֻכַּת אֶתקָֿרְבָּנָם יַקְרִיבוּ‎ 7:11, also 7:84; 7:88 (all P; see Di 7:20).

חנכי.def:
H2599. Chanoki

חֲנֹכִי‎ adjective, of a people of חֲנוֺךְ‎

4 only with article ׳הַח‎ = substantive collective Num 26:5.

חנם.def:
H2600. chinnam

חִנָּם‎ substantive, used chiefly in the accusative as

adverb (compare Assyrian annáma, in vain, DlK 7, Pr 44; from הֵּן‎, with aff. םָ֯‎, which is sometimes found in substantives proper, as סֻלָּם‎, and proper names, but is more particularly used with substantives applied adverbially, as רֵיקָם דּוּמָם, אָמְנָם, יוֺמָם‎: Sta§ 203 BaNB § 216) — literally out of favour; i.e.

a. gratis, gratuitously, for nothing, חִנָּם עָבַד‎ to serve for nought Gen 29:15; Job 1:9; Isa 52:3 to be sold (figurative) for nought 52:5; Exod 21:2, 11 חִנָּם יָצָא‎ to go out(from slavery) freely, for nothing, Num 11:5 which we used to eat in Egyptian for nought, Jer 22:13; 1Chr 21:24; in the Genitive 2Sam 24:24 חִנָּם עֹלוֺת‎ i.e. burnt-offerings which cost nothing (in the || 1Chr 21:24 the construction is changed).

b. for no purpose, in vain Prov 1:17; Mal 1:10: once חִנָּם אֶל‎ (compare אֶל‎ 7) Ezek 6:10.

c. gratuitously, without cause, undeservedly, especially of groundless hostility or attack, 1Sam 19:5 חִנָּם לְהָמִית‎ to slay David without cause, 25:31; Psa 35:7 (twice in verse); 109:3; 119:161 חִנָּם רְדָפוּנִי‎, Prov 1:11; 3:30; 23:29; Job 2:3 ח ׳לְבַלְּעוֺ‎ 9:17; 22:6; Ezek 14:23; Psa 35:19; and 69:5 חִנָּם שׂנְאַי‎ my haters without cause, Lam 3:52 חִנָּם אֹיְבַי‎; in the Genitive 1Kin 2:31 חִנָּם דְּמֵי‎ blood shed without cause (compare 1Sam 25:31), Prov 24:28 בְּרֵעֶ֑ךָ ח עֵד ׳אֲלתְּֿהִי‎, 26:2 ח ׳קִלְלַת‎ the causeless curse.

חנמאל.def:
H2601. Chanamel

חֲנַמְאֵל‎ proper name, masculine (perhaps = חנןאֿל‎) — Jeremiah's cousin, son of his uncle Jer 32:7-8, 9, compare ׳ח דֹּדִי‎ 32:12; ᵐ5‎ Αναμεηλ.

חנמל.def:
H2602. chanamel

[חֲנָמֵל‎] noun [masculine] only בַּחֲנָמַ֑ל‎ Psa 78:47 (on form see DrSm p. 98) as instrument of destroying sycomores (|| בָּרָד‎); meaning conjectural; ᵑ9 ᵐ5‎ frost.

חנן.def:
H2605. Chanan

חָנָן‎ proper name, masculine (gracious; compare Sabean חנן‎, Phoenician חנא‎) —

1 one of the warriors of David 1Chr 11:43.

2 one of the heads of families of Nethinim Ezra 2:46 = Neh 7:49.

3 names of Levites Neh 8:7; 10:11; 13:3.

4 chiefs of the people:

a. Neh 10:23.

b. Neh 10:27.

5 Benjamite name 1Chr 8:23, 38; 9:44 (compare proper name, of a location חָנָן בֵּית‎, Mishna חָנָן כְּפַר‎).

6 הָאֱלֹהִים אִישׁ‎ head of a prophetic guild, חָנָן בְּנֵי‎ Jer 35:4.

חננאל.def:
H2606. Chananel

חֲנַנְאֵל‎ proper name, masculine (E l; is gracious; compare Phoenician אלחנן חננבעל,‎, etc.) — name of a tower at Jerusalem Jer 31:38; Zech 14:10; Neh 3:1; 12:39.

חנני.def:
H2607. Chanani

חֲנָנִי‎ proper name, masculine (perhaps abbreviated from following); —

1 father of the prophet Jehu 1Kin 16:1, 7; 2Chr 16:7; 19:2; 20:34.

2 brother of Nehemiah Neh 1:2; 7:2.

3 a chief musician of David 1Chr 25:4, 25.

4 a chief musician in time of Nehemiah Neh 12:36.

5 a priest of Ezra's time Ezra 10:20.

חנניה.def:
H2608. Chananyah

חֲנַנְיָה חֲנַנְיָ֫הוּ,‎ proper name, masculine (׳י‎ hath been gracious) — ᵐ5‎ Ἀνανίας; חֲנַנְיָהוּ‎: (compare חנניהו‎ on Israel. Seal, GanneauJas Fev-Mars 1883, 128, No.1) —

1 father of a prince under Jehoiakim Jer 36:12.

2 captain of Uzziah's army2Chr 26:11.

3 chief of one of the divisions musicians of David 1Chr 25:23 = חֲנַנְיָה‎ 25:4. — חֲנַנְיָה‎:

4 a false prophet of Jeremiah's time Jer 28:1, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15 (twice in verse); 28:17.

5 one of the three companions of Daniel Dan 1:6-7, 11, 19.

6 grandfather of an officer of the guard in Jeremiah's time Jer 37:13.

7 a son of Zerubbabel 1Chr 3:19, 21.

8 a Benjamite 1Chr 8:24.

9 various post-exilic persons.

a. Ezra 10:28.

b. Neh 3:8.

c. Neh 3:30.

d. Neh 7:2.

e. Neh 10:24.

f. Neh 12:12, 41.

חֲנַנְיָה‎ proper name, masculine (= Biblical Hebrew id. 5); — Dan 2:17.

חנניהו.def:
H2608. Chananyah

חֲנַנְיָה חֲנַנְיָ֫הוּ,‎ proper name, masculine (׳י‎ hath been gracious) — ᵐ5‎ Ἀνανίας; חֲנַנְיָהוּ‎: (compare חנניהו‎ on Israel. Seal, GanneauJas Fev-Mars 1883, 128, No.1) —

1 father of a prince under Jehoiakim Jer 36:12.

2 captain of Uzziah's army2Chr 26:11.

3 chief of one of the divisions musicians of David 1Chr 25:23 = חֲנַנְיָה‎ 25:4. — חֲנַנְיָה‎:

4 a false prophet of Jeremiah's time Jer 28:1, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15 (twice in verse); 28:17.

5 one of the three companions of Daniel Dan 1:6-7, 11, 19.

6 grandfather of an officer of the guard in Jeremiah's time Jer 37:13.

7 a son of Zerubbabel 1Chr 3:19, 21.

8 a Benjamite 1Chr 8:24.

9 various post-exilic persons.

a. Ezra 10:28.

b. Neh 3:8.

c. Neh 3:30.

d. Neh 7:2.

e. Neh 10:24.

f. Neh 12:12, 41.

חֲנַנְיָה‎ proper name, masculine (= Biblical Hebrew id. 5); — Dan 2:17.

חנס.def:
H2609. Chanes

חָנֵס‎ proper name, of a location Isa 30:4 in Lower Egypt, on island in Nile, south of Memphis (|| צֹּעַן‎) = Egyptian Hnnstn [*–néns®], Assyrian –ininši; Herodotii. 137 Ἄνυσις, afterward Heracleopolis magna, now Ahnâs; see SteindBAS i. 602.

חנף.def:
H2612. choneph

חֹ֫נֶף‎ noun [masculine] profaneness — ח ׳לִעֲשׂוֺת‎ Isa 32:6 to practise profaneness (+ תּוֺעָה אָוֶַן, נְבָלָה,‎).

חנפה.def:
H2613. chanuppah

חֲנֻמָּה‎ (so Baer; van d. H חֲנֻפָךְ‎) noun feminine profaneness, pollution, Jer 23:15.

חנק.def:
H2614. chanaq

[חָנַק‎] verb strangle (Late Hebrew id., Aramaic חֲנַק‎, ; Arabic ); —

Niph`al Imperfect וַיֵּחָנַ֑ק‎ 2Sam 17:23 strangled himself (+וַיָּ֫מָת‎).

Pi`el participle מְחַנֵּק‎ Nahum 2:13 strangle, of lion strangling prey, figurative of Ninevitish king (object not expressed).

חנתן.def:
H2615. Channathon

חַנָּתֹן‎ proper name, of a location place in the tribe of Zebulun Josh 19:14; ᵐ5‎ Αμωθ, Αενναθωθ, ᵐ5‎L Αναθωθ; site unknown; according to Conder = Talm, Caphar Hanania (NbrGeogr. 176. 226) on the border of Upper and Lower Galilee, modern Kefr' Anân, SurveyWP i. 205, 207.

חסד.def:
H2616. chacad

I. [חָסַד‎] verb 1. be good, kind (Late Hebrew חָסַד‎ in derivatives חָסִיד‎ pious; Aramaic חֲסַד‎ be kind, mild (then beg), chiefly in derivatives חִסְדָּא‎ etc.; compare perhaps Arabic usually plural they assembled, followed by they combined for him, and took pains to shew him courtesy Lane574c, also RSProph. iv. n. 9 (and Schu AE see in Thes); > Thes and others Find primary meaning in eager zeal or desire (|| קנא‎), whence develop kindness (as above), and envy, Arabic , envy (verb & noun), Aramaic חֲסַד‎ be put to shame, , חַסֵּד‎ reproach, revile, v, II.חסד‎) — only

Hithpa`el Imperfect תִּתְחַסָּ֑ד עִםחָֿסִיד‎ thou shewest thyself kind 2Sam 22:26 = Psa 18:26. — On

Pi`el Prov 25:10 see II. חסד‎.

II. [חָסַד‎] verb be reproached, ashamed (Aramaism, see RSProph. iv, n. 9; Aramaic חֲסַד‎ be put to shame, , חַסֵּד‎ reproach, revile; חִסּוּדָא‎, shame, reproach, often in ᵐ5 ᵑ7‎ for חֶרְמָּה‎); — only

Pi`el Imperfect מֶּןיְֿחַסֶּדְךָ‎ Prov 25:10 lest he reproach thee, expose thee to shame.

חסדיה.def:
H2619. Chasadyah

חֲסַדְיָה‎ proper name, masculine (Yah is kind) son of Zerubbabel 1Chr 3:20.

חסה.def:
H2621. Chosah

חֹסָה‎ 1. proper name, masculine (refuge) — name of one of the Levitical doorkeepers of the temple 1Chr 16:38; 26:10-11, 16.

2. proper name, of a location place in the tribe of Asher Josh 19:29; site unknown; ᵐ5‎ Ιασιφ, A Σουσα, ᵐ5‎L Ωσα.

חסות.def:
H2622. chasuth

חָסוּת‎ noun feminine refuge; — מִצְרַיִם בְּצֵל וְהֶחָסוּת‎ Isa 30:3 (|| מַּרְעֹה מָעוֺז‎).

חסיד.def:
H2623. chasid

חָסִיד‎ adjective masculine kind, pious (so, as denoting active practice of חֶסֶד‎, kindness, Thes MV De and most, compare מָּקִיד קָצִיר,‎ etc.; > Hup on Psa 4:4 RVm who explained as passive reception of ׳י‎s חֶסֶד‎, compare אָסִיר שָֹׂכֹיר,‎ etc.; its use as attribute of God Jer 3:12; Psa 145:17, and the context 12:1; Micah 7:2 etc., favour active sense) — ׳ח‎ Psa 4:4 9t.; חֲסִידֶ֑ךָ‎ Deut 33:8; Psa 89:20; חֲסִידְי֯ךָ‎ 16:10; plural חֲסִידִים‎ 149:1; 149:5; suffix חֲסִידָ֑י‎ 50:5; חֲסִידָו֯‎ 1Sam 2:9 15t. suffixes; —

1 kind:

a. of man ח ׳עם תתחסד‎ with the kind thou shewest thyself kind 2Sam 22:26 = Psa 18:26.

b. of wing of ostrich חֲסִידָה אֶבְרָה אִם‎ Job 39:13 is it a kindly pinion? possibly with play on חֲסִידָה‎ feminine noun strok (is the ostrich kind like the stork?).

c. of God, only Jer 3:12; Psa 145:17.

2 pious, godly, either as exhibition of 'duteous love' toward God (CheOP 378), or (in view of rarity of such passages as Hosea 6:4, 6; Jer 2:2, and their possible ambiguity) because kindness, as prominent in the godly, comes to imply other attributes, and to be a designation of the godly character, piety:

a. as adjective — חסיד לא גּוֺי‎ a nation, not pious, = ungodly Psa 43:1.

b. elsewhere as substantive: singular, a pious man, the godly Psa 4:4; 12:2; 32:6; 86:2, || יָשָׁר‎ Micah 7:2; (thy) pious one(s) Psa 16:10 (Kt plural), 1Sam 2:9 (Qr plural) Prov 2:8, חֲסִידֶ֑ךָ אִישׁ‎ men of thy pious one Deut 33:8 (Moses, see Di; others, the man, thy godly one, i.e. Levi); plural the pious, godly, those of the people who were faithful, devoted to God's service, only in Psalter and chiefly, if not entirely, in late Psalms Psa 149:1; 149:5; his pious ones 30:5; 31:24; 37:28; 85:9; 97:10; 116:15; 148:14; 149:9; thy pious ones Psalm 52:11; 79:2; 132:9 2Chr 6:41; Psa 145:10; my pious ones 50:5, her (Zion's) pious 132:16. — (In Maccabean age, συναγωγὴ Ἀσιδαίων denoted, technically, the party of the pious, who opposed the Hellenization of the Judaea, see 1Macc 2:42; 7:13; 2 Macc 14:6 and CheOP 48, 56; so perhaps 116:15; 149:1; 149:5; 149:9.)

חסידה.def:
H2624. chasidah

I. חֲסִידָה‎ noun feminine stork (so called as kind and affectionate to its young) — Lev 11:19 = Deut 14:18; Psa 104:17; Jer 8:7; Zech 5:9.

חסיל.def:
H2625. chasil

חָסִיל‎ noun masculine a kind of locust (singular collective) always absolute ׳ח‎, and always as destructive; 1Kin 8:37 2Chr 6:28; Psa 78:46 (all || אַרְבֶּה‎), Josh 1:4; Joshua 2:25 (|| גָּזָם אַרְבֶּה, יָ֑לֶק,‎); compare הֶחָ ׳אֹסֶף‎ Isa 33:4 the gathering of the locust, in simile of despoiling of Assyria (|| גֵּבִים‎).

חסין.def:
H3220. yam

יָם‎390 noun masculineExod 14:27 sea (Phoenician ים‎; Arabic ; Palmyrene בימא‎ on the sea, VogNo. 79; on Assyrian iâmu, (¹mu), sea, see DlHWB 307 M-ACD 52 HptBAS i. 171 n.) — absolute יָם‎ 1Sam 13:5 +; יָ֫מָּה‎ Gen 28:14 +; construct יָם‎ 14:3 23t., also סוּף יָ֫מָּה‎ Exod 10:19, but always יַםסֿוּף‎ 13:18 22t.; suffix יַמָּהּ‎ Jer 51:36; plural יַמִּים‎ Judg 5:17 29t.; — sea: especially

1 Mediterranean Num 13:29 (E), 34:5 (P), Deut 1:7; Josh 5:1; 1 Kings 5:23 (twice in verse); Jonah 1:4 (twice in verse) + often; the Mediterranean is called also הַגָּדוֺל הַיָּם‎ Num 34:6-7, Josh 15:12, 47; Ezek 48:28 +, compare ׳הַיּ ׳גּ יָדַיִם וּרְחַב‎ Psa 104:25; הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ חַגּ ׳הַיָּם מְבוֺא‎ Josh 1:4; 23:4 (see Assyrian name of Mediterranean tiamtu rabitu ša sulmu šamši, etc., SchrNamender Meere. 171 ff.); ׳הַיּ ׳הַגּ הַלְּבָנוֺן אֶלמֿוּל‎ 9:1; ׳הַיּ הָאַחֲרוֺן‎ the hinder sea Deut 11:24; 34:2; Zech 14:8; Joel 2:20 (in the last two opposed to ׳הַיּ הַקַּדְמֹנִי‎, see below); of Mediterranean in particular part מְּלִשְׁתִּים יָם‎ Exod 23:31 (JE); יָפוֺ יָם‎2Chr 2:15 = יָפוֺא יָם‎ Ezra 3:7. **Of Mediterranean in plural Dan 11:45 [compare 8 d] Hi Ke Meinh Bev Dr (world-encircling seas Behrm).

2 יַםסֿוּף‎ 'Red Sea' (see סוּף‎) Exod 13:18 (compare 10:19), 15:4; Num 14:25; Deut 1:40; Josh 2:10; Judg 11:16 + often; also הַיָּם‎ Exod 14:2 (twice in verse); 14:9; Isa 51:10 (twice in verse); 63:11 +; probably also יָםמִֿצְרַיִם‎ 11:15; 'Red Sea' named or referred to approximately 66 t.; יִםסֿוּף‎ clearly of lanitic Gulf 1Kin 9:26 (compare 2Chr 8:17).

3 Dead Sea, מֶלַח יָם‎ sea of salt Gen 14:3; Num 34:3, 12; Deut 3:17; Josh 3:16; 12:3; 15:2, 5; 18:19; הָעֲרָבָה יָם‎ Deut 3:17; 4:49; Josh 3:16; 12:3; 2Kin 14:25; ׳הַי הַקַּדְמֹנִי‎ Ezek 47:18; Zech 14:8; Joel 2:29 (see above); simply יָם‎ Isa 16:8; Jer 48:32; — in יַעְזֵר יָם‎ 48:32 יָם‎ is textual error, strike out with Gf Gr Che Gie.

4 Sea of Galilee כִּנֶּרֶת יָם‎ Num 34:11; Josh 13:27; כִּנְּרוֺת יָם‎ 12:3; simply יָם‎ Deut 33:23.

5 more Generally sea, opposed to earth and (or) sky Gen 1:26, 28; 9:2 (P), Exod 20:11 (E), Hag 2:6 +? Job, Psalms, Isa2 etc.; Amos 6:12 read יָם בַּבָּקָר‎ for בקרים‎ (see בָּקָר‎); sea as under earth Psa 24:2 (compare Gen 1:10; 6:11; Exod 20:5 = Deut 5:3); figurative of flood of invaders, הַיָּם עַלבָּֿבֶל עָלָה‎ Jer 51:42.

6 of a mighty river, the Nile Nahum 3:8 (twice in verse); Isa 19:5 (|| נָהָר‎); compare בַּיָּם אֲשֶׁר הַתַּנִּין‎ 27:1 and בַּיַּמִּים כַּתַּנִּים‎ Ezek 32:2 (simile of Pharaoh); of Euphrates Isa 21:1; Jer 51:36 (according to Che Gf and others; Isa 21:1 perhaps better of Persian Gulf, see Di).

7 the great basin in temple-court, called the sea: מוּצָק אֶתהַֿיָּם וַיַּעַשׂ‎ 1Kin 7:23 2Chr 4:2; הַנְּחשֶׁת יָם‎ 2Kin 25:13; 1Chr 18:8; Jer 52:17; הַיָּם‎ alone 1Kin 7:24-25, 10t. Kings Chronicles + Jer 52:20.

8 combinations are:

a. shore of sea, sea-shore הַיָּם שְׂפַת‎ Josh 11:4; 1Kin 5:9, and in simile Gen 22:17; Judg 7:12; 1Sam 13:5; הַי ׳חוֺף‎ Josh 9:1; Ezek 25:16; יַמִּים חוֺף‎ Gen 49:13; Judg 5:17; compare הַיָּם חֶבֶל‎ Zeph 2:5 region by the sea; so 2:6 but dubious, see I. חֶבֶל‎

3. b. sand of the sea (shore) הַיָּם חוֺל‎ (in simile) Gen 32:13; 41:49; Hosea 2:1; Isa 10:22 + often (see חוֺל‎); לַיָּם גְּבוּל חוֺל‎ Jer 5:22.

c. הַיָּם לְשׁוֺן‎ tongue (arm or gulf) of sea Josh 15:5; 18:19; Isa 11:5.

d. עַדיָֿם מִיָּם‎ Amos 8:12; Zech 9:10; Psa 72:8, compare Micah 7:12; Zech 14:8 (twice in verse); Joel 2:20 (twice in verse); Dan 11:45.

9 = (west, west-word (originally sea-ward, from position of Mediterranean with reference to Palestine, and this sense still often perceptible): with other three points of compass Gen 13:14; 28:14 (J), Num 2:18; 35:5 (P), Deut 3:27; 1Kin 7:25; 1Chr 9:24; 2Chr 4:4; Ezek 42:19 6t. Ezekiel; Zech 14:4; Dan 8:4; Psa 107:3 (וּמִיָּם מִצָּפוֺן וּמִמַּעֲרָב מִמִּזְרָח‎; but read perhaps וּמִיָּמִן‎ from the south, Hu Pe Bi Che); opposed to east Josh 11:2; 16:6 16t. Ezekiel 48; west alone Gen 12:8 (J); יָם רוּהַ‎ Ezek 10:19 (J) west wind; לְ מִיָּם‎ westward Josh 8:9, 12, 13 +; יָ֫מָּה‎ westward, often of tabernacle Exod 26:22, 27; Num 3:23 +? Josh 5:1; 15:8, 10 etc., + often Ezekiel; הַיָּם דֶּרֶךְ‎ = westward Ezek 41:12; יָם גְּבוּל‎ western border Num 34:6 (twice in verse); Josh 15:2; מְּאַתיָֿם‎ west side Exod 27:12; 38:12; Num 35:5; Josh 18:14; הים דרך מְּאַת‎ Ezek 41:12 (see further פאה‎).

[יַם‎] noun masculine sea (ᵑ7‎ Syriac; see B יָם‎, √ ימם‎); — emphatic יַמָּא‎ Dan 7:2-3,.

חסיר.def:
H2627. chassir

חַסִּר‎ adjective lacking, wanting, deficient (compare Biblical Hebrew חָסֵר‎); — ׳ח‎ Dan 5:27.

חסל.def:
H2628. chasal

[חָסַל‎] verb finish off, consume (Aramaic חֲסַל‎ come to an end, Aph`el bring to an end) —

Qal Imperfect הָאַרְבֶּה יַחְסְלֶנּוּ‎ Deut 28:38 of locusts destroying crops.

חסם.def:
H2629. chasam

[חָסַם‎] verb stop up, muzzle (Late Hebrew id., חסום‎ muzzle; Aramaic חֲסַם‎ bind up fast) —

Qal Imperfect בְּדִישׁוֺ שׁוֺר תַחְסֹם לֹא‎ Deut 25:4 thou shalt not muzzle an ox when it is treading (i.e. threshing); Participle היא וְחֹסֶמֶת‎ Ezek 39:11 and it shall stop (the way of) the passers-by; but read אתהַֿגַּיְא וְחָֽסְמוּ‎ and they shall stop up the valley, Co see ᵐ5‎ Syrver Hi.

חסן.def:
H2632. chesen

[חֵ֫סֶן‎] noun masculine (royal) power; — emphatic חִסְנָא‎ Dan 2:37; suffix חִסְנִי‎ 4:27.

חסף.def:
H2635. chasaph

חֲסַף‎ noun [masculine] clay, potsherd (ᵑ7‎ id.; Christian-Palestinian Aramaic clay vessel, plural potsherds Schulth68, Syriac potsherd; חצְבָא ᵑ7‎, Late Hebrew חָצָב‎ clay vessel; Assyrian —aƒbu, id., jar (PS1238), whence Arabic pottery Frä169, but Sabean חסף‎ jar, acc to HomZMG Homxivi (1892), 532; compare Ethiopic jar (transposed; Di1265); see Biblical Hebrew [חַסְמַּם‎]); — ׳ח‎ absolute Dan 2:41 (׳ח מֶּחָר יְ‎), חֲסַ֑ף‎ 2:33. 2:42; construct ׳ח טִינָא‎ 2:41. 2:43; emphatic חַסְמָּא‎ 2:34. 2:35. 2:43.v: 45.

חספס.def:
H2636. chaspas

[חַסְמַּס‎] verb only Passive participle (scaled off) scale-like (apparent reduplication from *חסף‎ for חספסף‎, see Ew§ 158 c Ol§§ 214, 276 Ges§ 55, 6 Sta§ 291; Köi, 250 thinks euphon. for מְחֻסְמָּף‎; to be compare are Arabic , have scab, itch (Frey; but = ס‎ ?); Aramaic חַסְמָּא‎ potsherd, חַסְמְּנִיתָא‎ scale (of fish), scurf; Ethiopic scabiosus fuit Di587 and Exod 16:14) — hence מְחֻסְמָּס‎ scaled off, scale-like as Syrver ᵑ7‎ Thes Rob-Ges MV SS VB; — of the manna כַּכְּפֹר דַּק מְחֻסְמָּ֔ס דַּק‎ 16:14 a fine, scale-like thing, fine as the hoar-frost.

חסר.def:
H2639. cheser

חֶ֫סֶר‎ noun masculineProv 28:22 want, poverty — always absolute; ׳ח יְבֹאֶנּוּ‎ 28:22 want shall come to him; || כָּפָן‎ hunger Job 30:3.

חסרה.def:
H2641. Chasrah

חַסְרָה‎ proper name, masculine grandfather of Shallum who was husband of Huldah the prophetess (ᵐ5‎ A Εσσερη, ᵐ5‎L Ασερ) = חַרְחַם‎ 2Kin 22:14 (ᵐ5‎ Αραας, ᵐ5‎L Αδρα).

חסרון.def:
H2642. chesron

חֶסְרוֺן‎ noun masculine thing lacking, deficiency (LagBN 198) — only ׳ח לְהִמָּנוֺת לֹאיֿוּכַל‎ Eccl 1:15 what is lacking cannot be counted.

חף.def:
H2643. chaph

חַף‎ adjective clean — only אָנֹכִ֑י חַף שָפשַׁע בְּלִי֫ אֲנִי זַךְ‎ Job 33:9 I am pure, without transgression, I am clean (in speech of Elihu).

חפא.def:
H2644. chapha

[חָפָא‎] verb do secretly (properly cover, = חפה‎, q. v.); — only

Pi`el Imperfect וַיְחַמְּאוּד֗֗֗ברים‎ and they did things secretly 2Kin 17:9.

חפה.def:
H2646. chuppah

I. חֻמָּה‎ noun feminine canopy, chamber (as covering, enclosing) — absolute ׳ח‎ Isa 4:5; suffix תֻמָּתוֺ‎ Psa 19:6; חֻמָּתָהּ‎ Joel 2:16; —

1 canopy, ח ׳עלכֿלכּֿבוד‎ Isa 4:5 over all glory a canopy (for protection).

2 chamber, of bridegroom Psa 19:6 (metaphor of sunrising); of bride Joel 2:16 (|| חֶדֶר‎ of bridegroom).

חפז.def:
H2648. chaphaz

[חָפַז‎] verb be in trepidation, hurry, or alarm (Arabic hasten, incite, urge); —

Qal Imperfect יַחְמּוֺז‎ Job 40:23; תַּחְמְּזוּ‎ Deut 20:3; Infinitive construct suffix בְּחָפְזִי‎ Psalm 31:28; Psa 116:11; בְּחָמְּזָהּ‎ 2Sam 4:4; בְּחָפְזָם‎ 2Kin 7:15 Qr (Kt הֵחָֽפְזֵם‎); —

1 be in a hurry or alarm, of hurried flight 2Sam 4:4; 2Kin 7:15; Infinitive with ב‎ = noun, in my alarm Psa 31:23; 116:11; be alarmed Deut 20:3 (|| תיראו‎), Job 40:23 (of hippopotamus)

Niph`al Perfect נֶחְמָּ֑זוּ‎ Psa 48:6 (|| נִבְהֲלוּ‎) hurry away in alarm; so Imperfect יֵחָפֵז֑וּן‎ 104:7 (|| יְּנוּסוּן‎); Infinitive הֵחָֽפְזֵם‎ 2Kin 7:15 Kt see above; Participle נֶחְמָּז‎ 1Sam 23:26 hurried נ דוד ׳ויהי ללבת‎ and David became hurried to go.

חפזון.def:

or chatseb [חָצַב‎] חָצֵב‎ verb hew, hew out, cleave (Late Hebrew id., Aramaic חֲצַב‎; SI4. 6 participle plural החצבם‎; compare Phoenician מחצב‎ = Hebrew id.) —

חצה.def:
the‎, He, fifth letter; = numeral 5 in post-Biblical Hebrew; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

הֶ הָ, הַ, , הַּ‎ (on the use of these different forms, see the Grammars: e.g. Ges§ 35),

definite article, the (so Moabite, Phoenician (Schröd§ 62-4), Liµyan (Northwest Arabia) ha (DHMEpigr. Denkm. 4. 13. 58 ff.); not Assyrian Aramaic or Ethiopic: Arabic , of which, before dentals, sibilants, and liquids, the l is written but not pronounced, thus pronounced 'ash-shamsu = Hebrew הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ‎) — in General the use of the article in Hebrew is analogous to its use in Greek or German: but naturally there are applications peculiar to Hebrew (compare with what follows Ges§ 126 Ew§ 277): —

1 joined with substantives:

a. to mark a definite concrete object, as Gen 1:1 the heavens and the earth, הַמֶּלֶךְ‎ the king, etc. Never, however (as in Greek e.g. ὁ Πλάτων), before true proper names, though it is used with certain terms, chiefly geographical, of which the original appellative sense has not been lost, as הַבַּעַל‎ 'Baal,' literally 'the lord,' in plural הַבְּעָלִים‎ i.e. the various local Baals, הַשָּׂטָן‎ the Adversary Job 1:6ff. (as a proper name שָׂטָן‎, 'Satan,' only 1Chr 21:1); הַלְּבָנוֺן‎ (but not הַחֶרְמוֺן‎), הַיַּרְדֵּן‎ (but not הָאַרְנֹן‎), הַשָּׁרוֺן הַכַּרְמֶל,‎ the Sharon, הַשְּׁפֵלָה‎ the (Judaean) lowland, הַמִּישׁוֺר הַכִּכָּר,‎ the (Moabite) table-land, הָעַי הָעֲרָבָה,‎ '`Ai,' הַגִּבְעָה‎ 'Gibeah,' Judg 20:5ff., הַגָּלִיל‎ 'Galilee,' הַגִּלְעָד הַבָּשָׁן, הַגִּלְבֹּעַ, הַגִּלְגָּל,‎ (often), הַמִּסְגָּה הָעֹפֶל, הַיְשִׁימוֺן, הָרָמָה, הַמִּצְמָּה, הַשִּׁטִּים,‎.

b. with an adjective to denote one who exhibits a quality κατ’ ἐξοχήν, i.e. to express the comparative or superlative degree: so often, as Gen 1:16 הגדל המאור‎ the greater light, הקטן המאור‎ the lesser light, 27:1 הגדול בנו‎ = his elder son, 48:14 הצעיר‎ the younger, 42:13 הַקָּטֹן‎ the little one, i.e. the youngest, (of Joseph's brethren), Lev 21:10 מֵאֶחָיו הַגָּדוֺל‎ the chiefest of his brethren, Num 35:25 + הגדול הכהן‎ the chief priest, ב ׳הצעיר‎ the least among Judg 6:15, מן הצעירה‎ the least of 1Sam 9:21, ב ׳הַיָּפָה‎ the fairest among Song 1:8; 2Kin 10:3; Prov 30:30, compare Job 14:15.

c. with nouns which are not definite in themselves, but acquire their definition from the context, or from the manner in which they are introduced: thus (α) in the standing phrases הַיּוֺם‎ to-day, Gen 4:14; 21:26 + often; הַלַּיְלָה‎ to-night, 19:5; 30:15 +, once 1Sam 15:16 last night; so הַשָּׁנָה‎ this year, 2Kin 19:29; Jer 28:16; הַמַּעַם‎ this time, Gen 18:32 +. (β) הַנָּהָר‎ the river (κατ’ ἐξοχήν), i.e. the Euphrates; Exod 2:15 the well, the well namely of the district, Josh 8:11 the valley, 1Sam 17:3; 19:10 the wall, 19:13 the bed, 20:21 הַנַּעַר‎ the lad (whom Jonathan would naturally take with him), 20:34 the table. Hence occas. where a suffix would define the noun more precisely, as הַחֲמוֺר‎ 2Sam 19:27 + = my ass, Judg 3:20; 1Sam 1:9 הַכִּסֵּא‎ = his seat, Judg 4:15; 1Kin 22:35; 2Kin 10:15 + הַמֶּרְכָּבָה‎, 1Sam 18:10; 20:33 הַחֲנִית‎.

d. it is a peculiarity of Hebrew thought to conceive an object as defined by its being taken for a particular purpose, and thus by a kind of prolepsis to prefix the article to the noun denoting it: 1Sam 10:1 and Samuel took הַשֶּׁמֶן אֶתמַּֿךְ‎ literally the cruse of oil, not, however, a cruse which had been defined previously, but one rendered definiteby being now taken; in English idiom 'a cruse of oil,' 10:25 בַּסֵּפֶר‎ literally in the scroll or book, the one, namely taken for the purpose, i.e. in a scroll (so Exod 17:14; Num 5:23; Job 19:23), 21:10 בַּשִּׂמְלָה‎, Judg 4:18 בַּשְּׂמִיכָה וַתְּכַסֵּהוּ‎, 4:19; 7:13 הָאֹהֶל‎ a tent, 8:25; 9:48 אֶתהַֿקַּרְדֻּמֹּת‎ hatchets, 20:16 every one able to sling אֶלהַֿשַּׂעֲרָה בָּאֶבֶן‎ with a stone at a hair, 1Sam 6:8 בָּאַרְגָּז‎ (unless indeed the אַרְגָּז‎ was an understood appendage in every cart), Num 11:27 הַנַּעַר‎, a young man, 13:23 בַּמּוֺט‎ on a pole, Josh 2:15 בַּחֶבֶל‎ with a cord, 2Sam 17:17 השׁפחה‎ a girl (compare Dr1Sam 1:4; 19:13). Sometimes it is uncertain whether an article is to be referred to c or

d: e.g. 1Sam 2:13 his prong or a prong, 2Sam 18:9 his mule or a mule, etc.

e. with nouns that denote objects or classes of objects that are known to all, as הַמַּיִם הַזָּהָב, הַצּאֹן,‎; Gen 13:2 Abram was very rich וּבַזָּהָב בַּכֶּסֶף בַּמִּקְנֶה‎, Exod 31:4 וּבַכֶּסֶף בַּזָּהָב לַעֲשׂוֺת‎, Deut 14:26 and thou shalt lay out the money וּבַשֵּׁכָר וּבַיַּיִן וּבַצּאֹן בַּבָּקָר‎, 2Kin 9:30 עֵינֶיהָ בַּמּוּךְ וַתָּשֶׂם‎, in French 'elle mit du fard à ses yeux.' It is, however, remarkable that this usage depends mostly on the punctuation, הַלֶּחֶם הַיַּיִן, הַכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. (except as applied to denote definite quantities of gold, wine, etc., as Josh 6:24) being far less common than יַיִן כֶּסֶף,‎ etc., but לַכֶּסֶף בַּכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. being much more frequently than לְכֶסֶף בְּכֶסֶף,‎ etc.: for instances in which the article forms part of the consonantal text, see Gen 6:20; 7:8 + העוף‎ and הבהמה‎, Deut 8:3 הַלָּחֶם‎, 1Kin 5:8; 5:13; Isa 28:7 הַיַּיִן‎ and הַשֵּׁכָר‎, 60:17; Ezek 15:4, 7 הָאֵשׁ‎, Hab 2:5; Prov 20:1; Psalm 65:14 הַצּאֹן‎, Song 1:11; Eccl 7:12. compare below,

f. in comparisons, the object compared being, as a rule, not an individual as such, but one exhibiting the characteristics of a class: Isa 1:18 כַּתּוֺלָע כַּשָּׁנִים,‎ like scarlet, like crimson (both meant Generally), 5:24 יִהְיֶה כַּמַּק‎, 5:28 כַּצַּר‎ and כַּסּוּפָה‎, 10:14 כַּקֵּן‎, 13:8 כַּיּוֺלֵדָה‎ (as always with this word, e.g. 42:14; Psa 48:7), 11:7 כַּבָּקָר‎; + often (The usage is not, however, quite uniform, at least according to the punctuation: there occurs e.g. כְּקַשׁ‎ Job 41:21; Isa 47:14; כְּאַרְיֵה‎ Psa 7:3 and elsewhere: and we find both כַּלָּבִיא‎) Isa 5:29 and כְּלָבִיא‎ Hosea 13:8; כָּאֲרִי‎ Isa 38:13 and כַּאֲרִי‎ Num 24:9; כַּגִּבּוֺר‎ Isa 42:13 and כְּגבור‎ Job 16:14; etc.) Similarly Gen 19:28 הַכִּבְשָׁן כְּקִיטֹר‎ as the smoke of a furnace, Num 11:8, 12 אֶתהַֿיֹּנֵק הָאֹמֵן יִשָּׂא כַּאֲשֶׁר‎, Deut 28:29 (הָעִוֵּר‎), Judg 8:18b הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּנֵי כְּתֹאַר‎, 14:6 הַגְּדִי כְּשַׁסַּע‎ like (a lion's) rending a kid, 16:9; 1Kin 14:15; Zech 12:10 הַיָּחִיד עַל מִסְמֵּד כְּ‎ as mourning over an only child, 13:9 +. Where, however, the standard of comparison is not the class in General, but only a particular part of it, defined by a special epithet (whether adjective or verb), the article is naturally omitted: thus כַּמֹּץ‎ like chaff (in General) Isa 41:15, but עֹבֵר כְּמֹץ‎ like chaff passing away 29:5; כַּצֵּל‎ Job 14:2, but נָטוּי כְּצֵל‎ Psa 102:12; כַּקַּשׁ‎ Isa 40:24, but נִדָּף כְּקַשׁ‎ 41:2; כָּאַיָּל‎ 35:6, but, וג על תַּעֲרֹג ׳כְּאַיָּל‎ like a hind (that) longeth for streams of water Psa 42:2; כָּאֵשׁ‎ Isa 9:17, but יער תבער כְּאֵשׁ‎ like fire (that) kindleth a wood Psa 83:15; כֶעָשָׁן‎ Isa 51:6, but מֵאֲרֻבָּה כְּעָשָׁן‎ like smoke from a chimney Hosea 13:3: so Isa 62:1b Job 9:26; 11:16 עָֽבְרוּ כְּמַיִם‎ like waters (that) have passed by, etc.; Deut 32:2 a כַּטַּל כַּמָּטָר,‎, but 32:2 b עֲלֵיעֵֿשֶׂב כִּרְבִיבִים עֲלֵידֶֿשֶׁא, כִּשְׂעִירִים‎. Where the article is found, although a rel. clause follows (as Psa 1:4; 49:13; Isa 61:10), this is probably to be regarded not as limiting the class of object compared, but as describing it.

g. prefixed to generic nouns (in the singular) it designates the class, i.e. it imparts to the noun a collective force, as Exod 1:22 כָּלהַֿבֵּן‎ all (literally the whole of) the sons, כָּלהַֿבַּת‎ all the daughters, Lev 17:8, 10 מִןהַֿגֵּר‎ of the strangers, who sojourn in their midst, Num 21:7 הַגנָּחָשׁ‎ the serpents; Gen 14:13; Ezek 24:26; 33:21 הַמָּלִיט‎ those who escaped; Josh 6:7 + הֶחָלוּץ‎, v 9:13 הַמְאַסֵּף‎; 8:19 הָאוֺרֵב‎; 1Sam 13:17 הַמַּשְׁחִית‎; Micah 2:13; Isa 6:4 הַקּוֺרֵא‎ the choir of criers; 1Sam 24:14 הַקַּדְמֹנִי‎ the ancients; Eccl 7:26 אֶתהַֿאִשָּׁה‎ woman, and often with Gentile names, as הַיְבוּסִי‎ the Jebusites, וְהַמְּלֵתִי הַכְּרֵתִי‎ 2Sam 8:18 and elsewhere, הַדָּנִי‎ Judg 18:1 etc., הַלֵּוִי‎ the Levites, Num 3:20, 18:23; Mal 2:8; Psa 135:20 +.

h. with nouns denoting abstract ideas, especially the names of moral qualities (compare Greek ἡ δίκη, French la justice), chiefly in two cases — (α) where the article is recognizable in the consonantal text, exceptionally, when some emphasis or definiteness is intended, as Deut 7:9 והחסד הברית שׁומר‎; הזה החסד‎ 2Sam 2:5; 1Kin 3:6; והרחמים החסד את‎ Jer 16:5 (contr. Zech 7:9); הצדק‎ Isa 1:26; 61:3; Eccl 3:16; הַצְּדָקָה‎ Isa 32:17 (twice in verse) (contrast 32:16) Dan 9:7 (emphatic); הַדַּעַת‎ Hosea 4:6; הָאֱמֶת‎ Gen 32:11 (followed by אֲשֶׁר‎), Isa 59:15 (contrast 59:14) Zech 8:3, 19; הָאֱמוּנָה‎ Isa 11:5b (contr. va) Jer 7:28; הַחָכְמָה‎ Job 28:12, 20; הַחַיִּים‎ Gen 2:9 +; הָאַהֲבָה‎ Song 2:7; 3:5; 8:4, 7; הַשֶּׁקֶר‎ Jer 7:4, 8; 23:26; הַמָּוֶת‎ Isa 25:8; Ruth 1:17 +; הָרֶשַׁע‎ Psa 125:3; Eccl 3:16; הָרִשְׁעָה‎ Zech 5:8; הַחשֶׁךְ‎ Isa 60:2; Eccl 2:13; see also Deut 30:15, 19 (Jer 21:8), 1Kin 7:14; Jer 32:19; Mal 2:5 והשׁלום החיים‎, Psa 123:4; 130:4; Dan 9:9; 1Chr 29:11; 2Chr 1:12; Prov 31:30; Eccl 2:18, 17; 7:12, 19; 10:6; 11:10: but in all such cases אֱמֶת צֶדֶק, חֶסֶד,‎, etc. are far more common. (β) where the article depends on the punctuation, after prepositions, especially בְּ‎, but with much irregularity, as בַּחֶסֶד‎ Isa 16:5; Prov 20:28 (but ׳בְּח‎ Hosea 2:21; Prov 16:6), בַּצֶּדֶק‎ 25:5 (elsewhere always ׃בְּצ ׳בִּצְדָקָה‎ also always); בֶּאֱמֶת‎ and בֶּאֱמוּנָה‎ always; בַּשֶּׁקֶר‎ Isa 28:15 (but || כָּזָב‎, not הַכָּזָב‎) Jer 5:31; 13:25; 20:6; 23:14 (בְּשֶׁקֶר‎ 3:10; 29:9); בַּשָּׁלוֺם‎ Psa 29:11; Job 15:21 (elsewhere בְּשָׁלוֺם‎); Zech 12:4 to smite וּבַעִוָּרוֺן בַּשִּׁגָּעוֺן‎ (but Deut 28:28 וּבְעורון בְּשׁגעון‎), compare Gen 19:11; Deut 28:22; to enter with one בַּמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Job 9:32; 22:4 (but בְּמשׁפט‎ Psa 143:2), contrast also Prov 18:5; with 24:23; לַמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Isa 59:11; Psa 9:8 (but ׳לְמ‎ Isa 5:7; Psa 122:5); Prov 2:2; 7:4 לַחָכְמָה‎, (but never הַחכמה‎ in Proverbs 1-9, or indeed in the whole book); 2:3; 7:4 לַבִּינָה‎, Job 39:17 בַּבִּינָה‎ (but never הַבִּינָה‎); Prov 2:2-3,לַתְּבוּנָה‎ (but הַתְּבוּנָה‎ only 1Kin 7:14 emphatic); to perish בַּצָּמָא‎ Judg 15:18 +; Isa 29:21 בַּתֹּהוּ‎, 32:19 הָעִיר תִּשְׁמַּל בַּשִּׁמְּלָה‎ German in die Niedrigkeit sinkt die Stadt, 45:16 together they go בַכְּלִמָּה‎ (in die Schmach), 46:2 בַּשְּׁבִי‎ into captivity, 47:5 בַחשֶׁךְ בֹּאִי‎ (so always: never בְחשׁך‎). The living language may have used the article more readily after a preposition, where it did not lengthen the word by an entire syll.; still the disparity of usage between α and β makes it not improbable that the article in β is in many cases not original but due to the punctuators.

i. to mark the vocative: 1Sam 17:55 הַמֶּלֶךְ חֵינֿפשׁך‎ as thy soul liveth, O king, I do not know, 17:58 הַנַּעַר אתה מי בן‎ Whose son art thou, lad ? 2Sam 14:4 Help, O king ! 1Kin 18:26 עֲנֵנוּ הַבַּעַל‎, 2Kin 9:5 הַשָּׂר אֵלֶיךָ‎, Isa 42:18 שְׁמָ֑עוּ הֵַחרְשִׁים‎, Jer 2:31 וג רְאוּ אַתֶּם ׳הַדּֿוֺר‎, Ezek 37:4 הַיְּבֵשׁוֺת הָעֲצָמוֺת‎ O dry bones, Mal 3:9 כֻּלּוֺ הַגּוֺי‎ (Dr§ 198 Obs. 2).

N.B. In poetry, the article is frequently dispensed with before words which would naturally take it in prose: thus Psa 2:2; 2:8; 2:10 & often אֶרֶץ‎; 8:9; 18:10; 33:6 + שָׁמַיִם‎; (rarely in prose, Gen 1:8; 2:4; 1Kin 8:35); 21:2; 1Ki 45:14; 1Ki 45:16; 1Ki 61:7 and elsewhere מֶלֶךְ‎; 1Ki 66:6; 1Ki 72:8 + יָם‎; 1Ki 59:7; 1Ki 59:15 עִיר‎; Judg 5:2; Psa 18:44 עָם‎ etc.; 9:6; 9:17 & often רָשָׁע‎; Isa 1:2, 6, 21; 3:10-11, 11:6-7, 8.

2 With adjectives, participles, and demonstrative pronouns (אלה זאת, זה, הם, המה, היא, הוא,‎): namely

a. (so regularly) when the substantive qualified by these words is defined by it likewise, as הגדול המלך‎ = ὁ βασιλεὺς ὁ μέγας, Gen 2:12 ההוא הארץ‎, 20:1 הַזֶּה הַדָּבָר‎, Josh 2:3 אליך הבאים האנשׁים‎ = οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς σέ, Gen 13:5; 16:13; 24:65; 32:21; Judg 6:28; Isa 65:3-4, 5; 66:24; Psa 31:9. So also with adjectives & participles, if the substantive be defined by a suffix (as Deut 4:37 הַגָּדֹל בְּכֹחוֺ‎, 1Sam 8:14 הַטֹּבוֺת זֵיתֵיכֶם‎); and with a pronoun, if it be defined by a Genitive (as Deut 29:20; 1Sam 14:29; 15:14; 2Kin 6:32 הַזֶּה בֶןהַֿמְּרַצֵּחַ‎ this son of a murderer), but not if it be defined by a suffix, as Exod 10:1 אֵלֶּה אֹתֹתַי‎ (not הָאֵלָּה אתתי‎), Josh 2:14 זֶה דְבָרֵנוּ‎ this our word (not ׳ד הַזֶּה‎): see Dr§ 209 Obs. Similarly when the article with the participle has a resumptive force, Psa 33:15 (Psalm 14, he looketh forth from the place, &c.), לִבָּם יַחַד הַיֹּצֵר‎ he that formeth, etc., 19:11 מִזָּהָב הַנֶּחֱמָדִים‎ which (Psalm 10 b) are more desirable than gold, 49:7. (:6 b the iniquity of my aggressors surroundeth me), הַבֹּטְחִים‎ who trust in their riches, etc., Gen 49:21; Isa 46:6; 51:20; Job 6:16 + (see Dr§ 135. 7).

b. (rare) when the substantive qualified by the adjective or participle was felt to be sufficiently definite for its own article to be dispensed with, as sometimes with the word day Gen 1:31 השׁשׁי יום‎, 2:3 השׁביעי יום‎, Exod 12:15, 18; 20:10 (= Deut 5:14) Lev 19:6; 22:27: so with מָנוֺא‎ entrance Jer 38:14, שַׁעַר‎ Zech 14:10; חָצֵר‎ court 1Kin 7:8, 12; Ezek 40:28 and elsewhere; also in certain phrases (peculiar to P) where the substantive is defined by כל‎, as Gen 1:21 הַחַיָּה כָּלנֶֿפֶשׁ‎ all living souls, 1:28 הָרֹמֶשֶׂת כָּלחַֿיָּה‎ all living things that creep, etc., 7:21; 9:10; Lev 11:10, 46; further in isolated cases, hardly reducible to rule, 24:10; 1Sam 12:23 הַטּוֺבָה דֶּרֶךְ‎, 16:23 הָרָעָה רוּחַ‎, 2Sam 12:4 העשׁיר לְאישׁ‎ Jer 6:20; 17:2; Zech 4:7; Psa 104:18; Ezra 10:9 הַתְּשִׁיעִי חֹדֶשׁ‎ (quite exceptional in OT). (With pronouns this use is so rare that, where it occurs, it is dubious if the text be sound: 1Sam 17:12, 17; Jer 40:3 Kt Micah 7:11). And with the participle: 1Sam 25:10 הַמִּתְמָּֽרְצִים עֲבָדִים רַבִּים‎ many are the slaves who break away etc., Isa 7:20; Jer 27:3; 46:16 = 50:16 הַיּוֺנָה חֶרֶב‎ the oppressing sword, Ezek 2:3 (but ᵐ5‎ Co omit הגוים‎), 14:22; 32:22, 24; Psa 62:4; Prov 26:18; Judg 21:19 (very anomalous, read probably לַמְּסִלָּה‎). This usage is somewhat more frequently in the later parts of OT; and in Post-Biblical Hebrew it is very General (e.g. הָרַע יֵצֶד‎ the evil inclination): see further Dr§ 209.

c. with the participle, where the participle with the article forms really the subject: Gen 2:11 הַסּוֺבֵב הוּא‎ not 'it was encompassing,' but 'it is that which encompassed,' 45:12 הַמְדַבֵּר מִּי‎ my mouth is that which speaketh, Deut 3:21 הָראֹוֺת עֵינֶיךָ‎ thine eyes were those which saw, 4:3; 8:18 ὅτι οὗτος ἐστιν ὁ διδοὺς σοί, Isa 14:27; 66:9 (see Dr§ 135. 7).

3 The article is prefixed exceptionally — mostly in the latest Hebrew — with the force of a relative to the verb: Josh 10:24 אִתּוֺ הֶהָֽלְכוּא‎ that went with him, Ezek 26:17, הַהֻ֫לָּלָה הָעִיר‎, 1Chr 26:28 שְׁמוּאֵל הַהִקְדִּישׁ וְכֹל‎ and all that Samuel had dedicated, 29:8, 17; 2Chr 1:4 ַבּהֵכִין‎ in (the place) that he had prepared, 29:36; Ezra 8:25; 10:14, 17. According to the punctuation, it occurs similarly elsewhere, as Gen 18:21 הַשָבּאָה‎ (so 46:27; Job 2:11), 21:3 הַנּוֺלַדלֿוֺ‎, 1Kin 11:9 & Dan 8:1 הַנִּרְאָה‎, Isa 51:10 הַשָּׂ֨מָה֨‎, 56:3 הַנִּלְוָה‎, Ruth 1:22; 2:6; 4:3 (all הַשָּׁ֫בָה‎): but in all these passages, the change of a point, or even sometimes of an accent, would restore the normal participial construction (as לוֺ הַנּוֺלָד הַבָּשָאה,‎ compare Gen 48:5, הַנִּרְאֶה‎), which is, no doubt, what was intended by the original writers, and is recognised elsewhere by the Masora, e.g. 12:7; 35:1 הַנִּרְאֶה‎, 46:26 & Ruth 4:11 הַבָּאָ֣ה‎ (compare Ew§ 331 b Ges138, 3 b). Once, still more anomalously, before a preposition 1Sam 9:24 וְהֶעָלֶיהָ‎ (as though καὶ τὸ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς): but read probably וְהָאַלְיָה‎ and the fat tail, see Dr. (In Arabic also occurs, though very rarely, as a relative: WAG i. § CG 117). — On the anomalous use of the article with a word in the stative construct, see Grammars, as Ew§ 290 d, Ges§ 127 R. 4, also Dr§ 190-1.

חצור.def:
H2674. Chatsor

חָצֹר חָצוֺר,‎ proper name, of a location (LagBN 47 f.) — ᵐ5‎ Ασωρ, etc.;

1 a royal city of northern Canaan Josh 11:1 מֶלֶךְחֿ ׳יָבִין‎, compare 12:19, and Judg 4:2, 17; 1Sam 12:9; Josh 11:10 (twice in verse); 11:11, 13; 19:36; 2Kin 15:29; חָצֹר‎ 1Kin 9:15.

2 places in the Negeb:

a. Josh 15:23.

b. c. Josh 15:25 חָצוֺר הִיא חֶצְרוֺן וּקְרִיּוֺת חֲדַתָּה וחָצוֺר‎.

3 חָצוֺר‎ Neh 11:33 a Benjamite town, probably = חָצוֺר בַּעַל‎ q. v.

4 נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּו֯ר הִכָּה אֲשֶׂר חָצוֺר מַמְלְכוֺת‎ Jer 49:28, compare 49:30; 49:33, an Arabian locality, see WinerBW Hazor Gf Gie. — ח ׳עֵין‎ Josh 19:37, see below עַיִן‎.

חצור חדתה.def:
H2675. Chatsor

Chadattah חֲדַתָּה חָצוֺר‎ proper name, of a location (si vera lectio perhaps new Haƒôr, with Aramaic ת‎ in adjective) — Josh 15:25, see חָצוֺר‎; in Negeb of Judah, site unknown.

חצות.def:
H2676. chatsoth

[חָצוֺת‎] noun feminine (Infinitive form.) division, middle — only construct הַלַּיְלָה חֲצֹת‎ Exod 11:4 (J) = midnight; לַיְלָה חֲצוֺת‎ Job 34:20; Psa 119:62; in all = adverb. phrase of time (בְּ‎ omitted)

חצי.def:
H2678. chetsi

חֵ֫צִי‎ noun masculine2Kin 9:24 arrow (compare Arabic , Ethiopic id., Di134, and see Dr on 1Sam 20:36) — absolute הַחֵ֫צִי‎ 20:36-37, (twice in verse) + 20:38 Kt (Qr הַחִצִּים‎), perhaps also 20:21; 20:22 (so ᵐ5‎ We, for ᵑ0‎ plural הַחִצִּים‎), 2Kin 9:24; the usual form is חֵץ‎; see below

חציר.def:
H2682. chatsir

II. חָצִיר‎ noun masculineIsa 15:6 green grass, herbage, absolute חָצִיר‎ Num 11:5 16t.; construct חֲצִיר‎ Isa 37:27 = 2Kin 19:26; Psa 129:6; —

H2356. chor

III. חוֺר חֹר,‎ noun [masculine] hole; — absolute חֹר‎ 2Kin 12:10; Ezek 8:7 (strike out Co B etc.), חוֺר‎ Song 5:4, חֹרִים‎ 1Sam 14:11; construct חֹרֵי‎ Job 30:6; suffix חֹרָיו‎ Nahum 2:13, חֹרֵיהֶן‎ Zech 14:12; — hole in lid of chest 2Kin 12:10 (made by boring, נקב‎), in door Song 5:4; in wall Ezek 8:7 (see above); = eye-socket בְּח תִּמַּקְנָה ׳עיניו‎ Zech 14:12 (plague of enemies of Jerusalem); holes as hiding-places for men 1Sam 14:11, so also 13:6 Ew We Dr (for חוחים ᵑ0‎), dwelling of outcast people עָפָר חרי‎ Job 30:6; of dens of lions Nahum 2:13. — I.חֹר‎, see II. חור‎.

חר הגדגד.def:
H2735. Chor

Haggidgad גִּדְגָּד‎, in הַגּ ׳חֹר‎ see following & below חֹר‎.

I. חֹר‎ noun [masculine] hollow, only in הַגִּדְּגָּ֑ד חֹר‎ Num 33:32 hollow of Gidgad (see Di).

II., III. חֹר חוֺר,‎, (חוֺרִים‎) see below II., III. חרר‎.

חרב.def:
H2720. chareb

I. [חָרֵב‎] adjective dry, only feminine singular חֲרֵבָה‎ Lev 7:10 of meal-offering not moistened (with oil; P); חֲרֵבָה מַּתֿ‎ Prov 17:1 a dry morsel.

II. חָרֵב‎ adjective waste, desolate; — masculine singular absolute ׳ח‎ Jer 33:10 3t.; feminine singular חֲרֵבָה‎ Neh 2:3 2t.; feminine plural הֶחֳרֵבוֺת‎ Ezek 36:35, 38 (see Köi. 241); — of a city, defined בְּהֵמָה וּמֵאֵין אָדָם מֵאֵין‎ Jer 33:10, compare 33:12; also Neh 2:3, 17; הֶחֳרֵבוֺת הֶעָרִים‎ Ezek 36:35 (+ הַנֶּהֱרָסוֺת הַנְשַׁמּוֺת,‎; opposed to יָשָׁב֑וּ בְּצוּרוֺת‎).

חרבה.def:
H2723. chorbah

חָרְבָּה‎ noun feminine waste, desolation, ruin; — absolute ׳ח‎ Lev 26:31 15t. + Ezek 38:8 (strike out ᵑ6‎ Co) + 38:12 ᵐ5 חרבה‎ Co for חרבות‎; plural חֳרָבוֺת‎ Psa 9:7 11t. (Ezek 38:12, compare above); construct חָרְבוֺת‎ Isa 5:17 7t.; suffix חָרְבֹתַיִךְ‎ 49:19; חָרְבֹתָיו‎ Ezra 9:9; חָרְבֹתֶיהָ‎ Isa 51:3; חָרְבוֺתֶיהָ‎ 44:26; חָרְבוֺתֵיהֶם‎ Psa 109:10 2Chr 34:6 (compare חֶרֶב‎ and below); (chiefly mid. and late Hebrew Isa28t.; Jeremiah 10 t., Ezekiel 14 t. — including Ezek 38:8, q. strike out Co); —

1 waste, ruin, of cities of Israel Lev 26:31, 33 (H); Judah Isa 44:26; 49:19 (|| שֹׁמְמֹת‎), 58:12 (בנה‎), Jer 25:18; 27:17; 44:2, 6; Ezek 5:14; ruins of Jerusalem Isa 52:9; Dan 9:2; also Ezek 35:4; compare Mal 1:4 (with בנה‎), Ezek 36:10 (with בנה‎) 36:33 (id.); Egypt 29:9-10, (in both || שְׁמָמָה‎; חֹרֶב חרבות‎ in 29:10); ruin of temple Ezra 9:9; = ruined dwellings Psa 109:10; compare 2Chr 34:6, where read perhaps בְּחָרְבֹתֵיהֶם‎ for בתיהם בּחר‎ (see חֶרֶב‎ below III. חרב‎); Jer 22:5; in General ruins (si vera 1., see Di; object of בנה‎) Job 3:14; ח ׳כוס‎ Psa 102:7 an owl of a ruin.

2 of land: waste place amid ruins Isa 5:17, compare 51:3 (|| עֲרָבָה מִדְבָּר,‎); land a desolation Jer 7:34; 44:22; Ezek 25:13 (Edom) Jer 25:11; Isa 64:10 and Ezek 33:24, 27 (of Judah), compare 13:4, בח ׳כְשֻׁעָלִים‎ simile of the prophets; ׳הח הַשֹּׁמֵמוֺת‎ 36:4 (of Israel); of desolation of enemies of Israel Psa 9:7 (׳ח לָנֶ֫צַח‎); ׳ח עולם‎ = old ruins Isa 61:4 (with בנה‎); elsewhere perpetual ruin, desolation Jer 25:9; 49:13 (cities of Bosra); ׳ה מעולם‎ Ezek 26:20 (simile of Tyre).

חרבון.def:
H2725. cherabon

[חֵרָבוֺן‎] noun masculine drought, only plural construct קַ֫יִץ בְּחַרְבֹנֵי‎ Psa 32:4 metaphor of fever heat.

חרבונא.def:
H2726. Charbona

or Charbonah חַרְבוֺנָא‎ proper name, masculine eunuch of Ahasuerus Est 1:10 = חַרְבוֺנָה‎ 7:9 (Persian = donkey driver, Vulli, 668 b).

ךְַרְבּוֺנָה‎ proper name, masculine see foregoing.

חרבונה.def:
H2726. Charbona

or Charbonah חַרְבוֺנָא‎ proper name, masculine eunuch of Ahasuerus Est 1:10 = חַרְבוֺנָה‎ 7:9 (Persian = donkey driver, Vulli, 668 b).

ךְַרְבּוֺנָה‎ proper name, masculine see foregoing.

חרג.def:
H6697. tsur

I. צוּר‎ noun masculineJob 29:6 rock, cliff; — ׳צ‎ absolute Exod 17:6 +, construct Deut 8:15 +; suffix צוּרִי‎ 2Sam 22:3, etc.; plural צֻרִים‎ Num 23:9 +, צוּרוֺת‎ Job 28:10; construct צוּרֵי‎ 1Sam 24:3 (Gi v.24:2); —

1. a. rocky wall, cliff, Exod 17:6 (twice in verse) (E), Deut 8:15 (׳צ הַחַלָּמִישׁ‎), Isa 48:21 (twice in verse); Psa 78:15; 78:20; 105:41; 114:8; (|| חַלָּמִישׁ‎); בַצּ ׳בּוֺא‎ Isa 2:10, צֻרִים בִּמְעָרוֺת‎ 2:19, הַצּ ׳בְּנִקְרוֺת‎ 2:21, compare Exod 33:21-22, (JE); yielding honey (from its clefts) Psalm 81:17 (compare Deut 32:13; Dy PerlesAnal. 34 We read צוּף‎); as look-out Num 23:9 (JE), home of goats 1Sam 24:3 (Gi v.24:2), snow-covered Jer 18:14; bearing (olives for) oil Deut 32:13 (צ ׳חַלְמִישׁ‎), Job 29:6; resort of homeless 24:8, pierced by miners 28:10, compare perhaps אוֺפִיר בְּצ ׳שִׁית נְחָלִים‎ 22:24 deposit (thy) gold in the rock of the wadys (most below צֹר‎ pebble); as quarry, figurative of Abraham as ancestor of Israel Isa 51:1; place of security 1Chr 11:15, ׳צ הַמִּישׁוֺר‎ Jer 21:13 (of city), figurative Psa 27:5; 61:3; symbol of firmness Nahum 1:6; Job 14:18; 18:4; enduring material 19:24.

b. rock with flat surface 2Sam 21:10; Prov 30:19.

c. block of stone, boulder Judg 6:21; 13:19 (as altar); compare מִכְשׁוֺל צוּר‎ Isa 8:14 (|| אֶבֶן נֶגֶף‎).

d. rock with specific name, ׳צ עוֺרֵב‎ Judg 7:25; Isa 10:26.

2. a. figurative of God (33 t.) as support and defence of his people (often || ׳י אֱלֹהִים,‎, etc.), ׳צ מָעֻזֵּךְ‎ Isa 17:10, ׳צ מָעוֺז‎ Psa 31:3, ׳צ עֻזִּי‎ 62:8, ׳צ מָעוֺן‎, 71:3, ׳צ יְשֻׁעָתוֺ‎ Deut 32:15 compare 2Sam 22:47b (but strike out, see || Psa 18:47), 89:27; 95:1, ׳צ וִישׁוּעָתִי‎ 62:3; 62:7, ׳צ מַחְסִי‎ 94:22; ׳צ יִשְׂרָאֵל‎ Isa 30:29; 2Sam 23:3 (personified), צוּרִי‎ Psa 18:3; 18:47 = 2Sam 22:3, 47a, >Bible:Psalm 19:15>; Psa 28:1; Psalm 92:16; 144:1, ׳צ לְבָבִי‎ 73:26, צוּרֵנוּ‎ Deut 32:31, צוּרָם‎ 32:30; Psa 78:35; with בְּ‎ essent. ׳צ עוֺלָמִים י ׳בְּיָהּ‎ Isa 26:4 (compare Psa 62:8; see ב‎ I. 7 c); as

proper name, of deity (the Rock Deut 32:4, 18 (׳צ יְלָֽדְךָ‎), 32:37; Hab 1:12, +(perhaps) Psa 75:6 (read בַּצּוּד‎, see צַוָּאר‎; see also מְּדָהצוּר‎).

b. of a heathen god Deut 32:31, compare Isa 44:3, א ׳מִבַּלְעֲדֵי צוּר מִי‎ 2Sam 22:32 || Psa 18:32, compare 1Sam 2:2. — See also צוּר בֵּית‎ and הַצֻּרִים חֶלְקַת‎. — Psa 89:44 see צֹד‎ below III. צרר‎, 49:15 see צוּרָה‎ below III. צור‎. above

חרגל.def:
H2728. chargol

חַרְגֹּל‎ noun [masculine] a kind of locust (Late Hebrew id.; Aramaic , חַרְגּוֺלָא‎; (Dozy), all = locust; swarm of locusts (Frey)) — only Lev 11:22 (P) in list of edible insects, || חָגָב סָלְעָם, אַרְבֶּה,‎.

חרד.def:
H2730. chared

חָרֵד‎ verbal adjective of foregoing, trembling; — חָרֵד‎ Judg 7:3 3t.; חֲרֵדִים‎ Isa 66:5; Ezra 10:3 — trembling (from fear), absolute Judg 7:3 (|| ירא‎), 1Sam 4:13 (subject לִבּוֺ‎, followed by עַל‎, for, in behalf of); in awe and reverence, at word of God, sq, בְּ‎ Ezra 9:4; Isa 66:2 (followed by עַל‎), 66:5 (followed by אֶל‎); compare ׳ח אל ׳בְּמִצְוַת‎ Ezra 10:3.

חרדה.def:
H2731. charadah

I. חֲרָדָה‎ noun feminine trembling, fear, anxiety — חֲרָדָה‎ Gen 27:33 5t. + Ezek 38:21 (read for הָרַי‎, B Co compare Dr 1Sam 14:15); construct חֶרְדַּת‎ 14:15; Prov 29:25 (see LagBN 113); plural חֲרָדוֺת‎ Ezek 26:16; —

1 trembling, quaking (of terror ascribed to supernatural cause) 1Sam 14:15 (twice in verse) (hence ׳ח אלהים‎ see Dr; || וַתִּרְגַּזהֿארץ‎) compare Ezek 38:21 (see above); Dan 10:7; ח ׳קול‎ Jer 30:5 voice of trembling; followed by Genitive object ׳ח אָדָם‎ Prov 29:25 trembling before man; opposed to pleasure Isa 21:4; tremblings (plural) Ezek 26:16 under figure of garment (׳ח ילבשׁו‎), of effect on coast-princes of fall of Tyre.

2 anxious care 2Kin 4:13, accusative of congnate meaning with verb with חָרַד‎.

חרדי.def:
H2733. Charodi

חֲרֹדִי‎ adjective, of location only with article ׳הַח‎, of Harod 2Sam 23:25 a (see Dr and Judg 7:1); = הַהֲרוֺרִי‎ 1Chr 11:27 (read הַהֲרוֺדִי‎); also 1Sam 23:25b but probably not Genuine; not in ᵐ5‎ or 1Chr 11:27 (see Dr and אֱלִיקָא‎ above).

חרה.def:
H2734. charah

חָרָה‎ verb burn, be kindled, of anger (Aramaic חרי‎ Pa`el cause, fire to burn (rare); Zinjirli חרא‎ anger, NöZMG 1893, 98. 103; Arabic burning sensation, in throat, etc., from rage and pain) —

Qal Perfect ׳ח‎ Gen 4:6 20t.; Imperfect יֶחֱרֶה‎ Exod 32:11 2t.; יִ֫חַר‎ Gen 18:30 7t.; וַיִּ֫חַר‎ 4:5 46t.; Infinitive absolute חָרֹה‎ 1Sam 20:7; construct חֲרוֺת‎ 2Sam 24:1; Psa 124:3; —

1 of man:

a. אף חרה‎ (one's) anger was kindled, burned Gen 39:19; Num 22:27 (J), Exod 32:19, 22 (JE), Judg 9:30; 14:19; 1Sam 11:6; Job 32:2, 5; with בְּ‎ against Gen 30:2 (E), 44:18 (J), 1Sam 17:28; 20:30; 2Sam 12:5; 2Chr 25:10; Psa 124:3; Job 32:2-3, with אֶל‎ Num 24:10 (E).

b. impersonal, אף‎ omitted; לְ חרה‎ it was kindled for (him) he burned with anger Gen 31:36 (E), 4:5-6, 34:7; Num 16:15 (J), 1Sam 15:11 (read perhaps וַיֵּצֶר‎, Weir in Dr), 18:8; 20:7 (twice in verse); 2Sam 3:8; 6:8 = 1Chr 13:11; 2Sam 13:21; 19:43; Nehemiah 3:33; Neh 4:1; 5:6; Jonah 4:1, 4, 9 (twice in verse); insert לדוד ויחר‎ 2Sam 11:22 ᵐ5‎ We Dr; ׳ח בְּעֵינֵי‎ Gen 31:35; 45:5 (E).

2 of God:

a. ׳ח אף‎ Exod 22:23; Num 22:22 (E), 11:1, 10; 32:10 (J); with בְּ‎ Exod 4:14; 32:10; Num 12:9; Deut 31:17 (J), 6:15; 7:4; 11:17; 29:26; Josh 23:16 (D), Judg 6:39; 2Sam 6:7 = 1Chr 13:10; Hosea 8:5; 2Kin 23:26; 2Chr 25:15; Job 42:7; בְּעַם‎ Exod 32:11; Num 11:33 (J), Isa 5:25; Psa 106:40; בישׂראל‎ Num 25:3; 32:13 (JE); Judg 2:14, 20; 3:8; 10:7; 2Sam 24:1; 2Kin 13:3; ישׂראל בבני‎ Josh 7:1 (R); אף בנהרים,‎ omitted, Hab 3:8; with עַל‎ Zech 10:3.

b. לְ חרה‎ Gen 18:30, 32 (J) 2Sam 22:8 = Psa 18:8. —

Note: חרה‎ not in HP (who use קצף‎); nor in Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Isa2, Proverbs or poetry of Job.

Niph`al Perfect נִחֲרוּֿ‎ followed by בְּ‎ Song 1:6 (according to Böii. 379 De Kö1. 551) be angry with; Participle בְּ הַנֶּחֱרִים ׳כֹּל‎ all that are incensed against (thee) Isa 41:11, so 45:24.

Hiph`il Perfect הֶחֱזִיק הֶחֱרָה‎ Neh 3:20 burned with zeal (?) in repairing, but ᵐ5‎ omit החרה‎; probably dittograph; Imperfect אַמּוֺ עָלַי וַיַּחַר‎ Job 19:11 and kindled his anger against me.

Hithpa`el Imperfect תִּתְחַר אַל‎ Psa 37:1; 37:7; 37:8; Prov 24:19 heat oneself in vexation. — The following forms are somewhat dubious: Imperfect2masculine singular אֶתהַֿסּוּסִים תְּתַחֲרֶה אֵיךְ‎ Jer 12:5 how canst thou hotly contend (in a race) with the horses ? Participle בָאָ֑רֶז מְתַחֲרֶה אַתָּה כִּי‎ 22:15 because thou strivest eagerly (to excel) in cedar; explained as Tiph`el by Thes Ges§ 55, 5 Ew§ 122 a Ol§ 255 a Sta§ 159 b Köi. p. 557 and others, and regarded by most as a rare causative stem; but ag. existence of Tiph`el see BaNB § 180 a; ZMG 1894, 20; Ba regards the form as denominative (from a noun formed by ת‎ preform., compare Aramaic contention); SS would point as Hithpa`el [compare Syriac contend with, contention], although meaning of Hithpa`el is different, see above

חרהיה.def:
H2736. Charhayah

חַרְחֲיָה‎ (van d. H חרהיה‎), proper name, masculine (√ and meaning unknown) — father of one of the builders of the wall, Nehemiah's time Neh 3:8.

חַרְחֻר חַרְחוּר,‎ see below I. חרר‎.

חרוזים.def:
H2737. charuz

[חָרוּז‎] noun [masculine] string of beads, only plural בַּחֲרוּזִים צַוָּארֵךְ‎ Song 1:10 thy neck (is comely) with strings of beads.

חרול.def:
H2738. charul

חָרוּל‎ noun [masculine] a kind of weed, perhaps chickpea (cicercula), see Löwp. 153 (Syriac fodder for horses; ᵑ7‎ Prov 24:31 gives חוּרְלָא‎) — absolute ׳ח‎ Job 30:6; Zeph 2:9; plural חֲרֻלִים‎ Prov 24:31; — as growing in devastated land, collective Zeph 2:9; in vineyard of slothful, plural ח פניו ׳כִּסּוּ‎ Prov 24:31 (|| קִמְּשׂגִים‎); as sole shelter of certain outcast peoples Job 30:7 (שִׂיחִים‎).

חרומף.def:
H2739. Charumaph

חֲרוּמַף‎ proper name, masculine father of one of the builders of the wall Neh 3:10.

חרז‎ (√ of following; Late Hebrew חֲרַז‎ string together, especially jewels or pearls; Aramaic חֲרַז‎ id.; id.; Arabic sew or stitch, beads strung together, neck-ornament).

חרון.def:
H2740. charon

חָרוֺן‎ noun masculine (burning of) anger (compare LagBN 204 Anm. * *) — ׳ח‎ Ezek 7:12 2t.; construct חֲרוֺן‎ Num 25:4 33t.; suffix חֲרוֺנִי‎ Ezek 7:14 (Co חרון‎), חֲרוֺגוֺ‎ Psa 2:5; חֲרֹנְךָ‎ Exod 15:7; plural suffix חֲרוֺנֶי֑ךָ‎ Psa 88:17; — always of God's anger (see note, below), אף חֲרוֺן‎ Exod 32:12; Num 25:4; 32:14; Josh 7:26 (J), Deut 13:18; 1Sam 28:18; 2Kin 23:26; 2Chr 28:11, 13; 29:10; 30:8; Ezra 10:14; Hosea 11:9; Nahum 1:6; Zeph 2:2; 3:8; Isa 13:9, 13; Jer 4:8, 26; 12:13; 25:37-38, 30:24; 49:37; 51:45; Jonah 3:9; Psa 69:25; 78:49; 85:4; Job 20:23; Lam 1:12; 4:11; אף‎ omitted, Exod 15:7 (song), Neh 13:18; Psa 2:5; Ezek 7:12 (strike out Co), 7:14; plural bursts of burning anger Psa 88:17. —

Note: כְּמוֺחָֿרוֺן‎ Psa 58:10 burning anger ᵑ9 ᵐ5‎ Jerome AV Bae Che; but Thes MV SS DeW Ew Ol Pe, something burning, e.g. thorns, antith. green thorns; Hengst De cooked flesh, antith. raw; Jer 25:38 ח ׳מפני הַיּוֺנָה‎ because of the fierceness of the oppressor (? AV) would then be the only use of the word of other than God's anger; here ᵑ7 ᵐ5‎ Ew Hi Gf Ke Che Gie RV rightly read חרב‎ oppressing sword (as 46:16; 50:16). חרון‎ is not used in H P D2 or E (except song, Exod 15:7) of the Hexateuch; nor in Ezekiel except Ezek 7:12 (strike out Co), 7:14.

חרונים.def:
H2773. Choronayim

חֹרֹנַיִם חֹרוֺנַיִם,‎ proper name, of a location (possibly two hollows, caves, ravines, see חוֺרֹן בֵּית‎) — חרונים דֶּרֶךְ‎ Isa 15:5; Jer 48:3, חֹרוֺנָ֑יִם מוֺרַד‎ 48:5, חֹרֹנַיִם‎ 48:34, city of Moab; = MI31, 32 חורנן‎ (i.e. probably חוֺרֹנֵן‎); ᵐ5‎ Αρωνιειμ, Ωρωνσιμ. — On ᵐ5 חֹרֹנַיִם‎ Josh 13:10-11, 2Sam 13:34 see We Dr and חוֺרֹן בֵּית‎.

חרופי.def:
H7145. Qorchi

קָרְחִי‎ adjective, of a people of קֹרַח‎

2; always with article; 1Chr 9:31; as substantive collective Exod 6:24; Num 26:58; plural הַקָּרְחִים‎ 1Chr 9:19; 12:7 (van d. H. v.12:6). 26:1; בְּנֵי הַקָּרְחִי‎ 26:19; הַקָּרְחִים בְּנֵי‎2Chr 20:19.

II. קרח‎ (√ of following; meaning unknown).

חרוץ.def:
H2782. charats

I. חָרַץ‎ verb cut, sharpen, decide (Late Hebrew id., cut in, decide, Aramaic in derivatives; Assyrian —arâƒu, dig, decide, —ariƒu, trench, ZehnpfBAS i. 502; Phoenician חרץ‎ decision, HoffmAGG xxxvi, May 1889, 11) —

Qal Perfect3masculine singular ׳ח‎ Josh 10:21; חָרָ֑צְתָּ‎ 1Kin 20:40; Imperfect יֶחֱרַץֿ‎ Exod 11:7; 2masculine singular תֶּחֱרָ֑ץ‎ 2Sam 5:24; Passive participle חָרוּץ‎ Isa 10:22; Lev 22:22; plural חֲרוּצִים‎ Job 14:5 (see also חָרוּץ‎ below); —

1 cut, mutilate Lev 22:22 (יַבֶּלֶת אוֺ אוֺחָֿרוּץ שָׁבוּר אוֺ עַוֶּרֶת‎).

2 sharpen, figurative the tongue, יֶח לְ׳לֹא לְשֹׁנוֺ כֶּֿלֶב‎ Exod 11:7 (J), i.e. utter no sound against Israel, Josh 10:21.

It has three peaks; and the names חרמון‎ and שׂניר‎, distinguished in 1Chr 5:23; Song 4:8, may refer to two of these peaks; חֶרְמוֺנִים‎ Psa 42:7 probably refers to these different peaks (see RobBR iii. 357 BädPal 301). Stadt Harran, 1892.
