2 burn, of bones in fever Psa 102:4 (כְּמוֺקֵד‎, compare

Qal Job 30:30); be parched, of throat ׳נח גרוני‎ Job 69:4. — Isa 41:11; 45:24; Song 1:6 see חרה‎.

Pilpel Infinitive לְחַרְחַררִֿיב‎ Prov 26:21 to kindle strife.

חררים.def:
H2788. charer

[חָרֵר‎] noun [masculine] parched place (Arabic , BdPal 196), only plural absolute חֲרֵרִים‎; ׳ח במדבר‎ Jer 17:6 (|| עֲרָבָה‎) figurative of life of godless.

חרש.def:
ב‎

בּ ב,‎, Bêth, 2nd letter; post Biblical Hebrew = numeral 2 (and so in margin of printed MT); ב֟‎ = 2000; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

I. בְּ‎,

preposition in (Moabite בּ‎, Syriac , Arabic , Ethiopic ) before tone-syllables in certain cases (Ges§ 102. 2) בָּ‎, with suffix בִּי‎; בְּךָ‎ (Ex 7:29; 2Sam 22:30; Psa 141:8 בְּכָה‎), in pause and feminine בָּךְ‎; בּוֺ‎ (once, Jer 17:24 Kt בֹּה‎), בָּהּ‎; בָּנוּ‎; בָּכֶם‎, [בָּכֶן‎]; בָּם בָּהֶם,‎ [also בָּהֵ֫מָּה‎ Exod 30:4; 36:1; Hab 1:16], בָּהֶן‎ 1Sam 31:7; Isa 38:16; Ezek 42:14 [15 times בָּהֵן‎ (FrMM 235), and thrice, Leviticus 5:22; Num 13:19; Jer 5:17, בָּהֵ֫נָּה‎]. Preposition denoting properly in, Greek ἐν, but applied in many derived and figurative significations. The senses expressed by בְּ‎ are grouped by the Rabbis in three classes, הַכְּלִי בֵּית‎ Beth vasculi, וְהַנְּגִיעָה הַדִּיבִּוּק בֵּית‎ Beth coniunctionis et viciniae, הָעֵזֶר בֵּית‎ Beth auxilii; and the same arrangement may be followed here, though the limits between the three classes are not clearly defined, and they sometimes overlap one another.

I. In:

1 strictly, of position in a place (which often is expressed more precisely by בְּתוֺךְ בְּקֶרֶב,‎), as בַּבַּיִת‎ in the house, בָּעִיר‎ in the city, בַּדּוּד‎ in the pot, בָּאָרֶץ‎ in the land, etc. constantly. Hebrew idiom also says בָּהָר‎ in the mountain Exod 24:18 etc., even in cases where we could hardly avoid saying on, as 1Kin 11:7; 19:11: so בְּחֹרֵב‎ Deut 1:16 and elsewhere; הָהָר בְּראֹשׁ‎ Exod 24:17; Psa 72:16. Preceded by a verb of motion (especially עָבַר‎) בְּ‎ = through, as Gen 12:6 and Abram passed through בָּאָרֶץ‎ in the land = passed through it, 13:17; 2Sam 24:2 +; in (= through) a gate, Isa 62:10; Jer 17:19; Micah 2:13. Figurative to speak בְּאָזְנֵי‎ in the ears of ...; to be good (or evil, etc.) בְּעֵינֵי‎ in the eyes of ...

2 of presence in the midst of a multitude, among, Exod 14:28 there was not left בָּהֶם‎ among them even one, Lev 26:36; 2Sam 15:31 Ahitophel בַּקֹּשְׁרִים‎ is among the conspirators, 2Kin 18:5 יְהוּדָה מַלְכֵי בְּכֹל‎. So בְּךָ‎ in thee (of Israel, collective) Deut 7:14; 15:4, 7; 18:10; 23:11; 28:54 (different from עִמָּ֑ח‎ beside thee Lev 25:35). — Specifically

a. of an individual, implying eminency among: Josh 14:15; Jer 46:18 Tabor among the mountains, 49:15; Prov 30:30; Song 1:8 בַנָּשִׁים הַיָּפָה‎ the fair one (= the fairest) among women, Lam 1:1: compare Luke 1:42. On 1Sam 17:12 see Dr.

b. hence with some verbs, when the action refers to only a part of the object, as בְּ הִכָּהַ‎ to smite among... i.e. to smite some of... (different from הִכָּה‎ with accusative); בְּ הָרַג‎ Psa 78:31; בְּ נָשָׂא‎ to bear in, i.e. to share in bearing, Num 11:17 and elsewhere; בְּ בָּנָה‎ to build in or at Zech 6:15; Neh 4:4; בְּ עָשָׂה‎ Exod 5:9; בְּ עָמֵל‎ to labour on Jonah 4:10; בְּ שָׁתָה בְּ, אָכַל‎ to eat or drink of Judg 13:16; Prov 9:5; בְּ חָלַק‎ to give a share in Job 39:17.

c. specifying the parts of which a whole consists (especially in P) Gen 7:21; 8:17; 9:10, 16; 17:23; Exod 12:19; Num 31:11, 26; Hosea 4:3.

3 with reference to the limits enclosing a space, within: Exod 20:10 בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ‎ within thy gates, Isa 56:5 בְּחוֺמוֺתַי‎ within my walls.

4 often pregn. with verbs of motion, when the movement to a place results in rest in it, into: after בָּא‎ Gen 19:8; Isa 19:23; נָתַן‎ Gen 27:17; שָׁלַח‎ to send Lev 16:22; in among Josh 23:7, 12; 1Kin 11:2. — Hosea 12:7 (an extreme case) בְּ שׁוּב‎ to return (and rest) in thy God, 1Sam 16:3 (unless לַזָּבַ֑ח‎ should be read, as 16:7). — בְּעַיִן עַיִן‎ (with) eye (looking) into eye Num 14:14; Isa 52:8; בְּפָנִים מָּנִים‎ Deut 5:4; פְ ׳עֵינֵי בְּ‎ the eyes of ... are upon, both in favourable (11:12; Psa 101:6) and hostile (Amos 9:8; Job 7:8) sense.

5 applied to time, as Gen 1:1 בְּרֵאשִׁית‎ in the beginning; 2:2 הַשְּׁבִיעִי בַּיּוֺם‎ on the seventh day; Judg 10:8 הַהִיא בַּשָּׁנָה‎ in that year; & constantly.

6 of a state or condition, whether material or mental, in which an action takes place: so often, בְּשָׁלוֺם‎ in peace Gen 15:15; בַּצָּרָה‎ in distress Psa 91:15; בְּתֻמּוֺ הָלַךְ‎ to walk in his integrity; Exod 5:19 בְּרָע‎ in evil case.

7 בְּ‎ introduces the predicate, denoting it as that in which the subject consists, or in which it shews itself (the Beth essentiae, — common in Arabic, especially with a participle or adjective and in a negative sentence: Qor 2:79 and God (appears) not as one remiss; 2:7 and they are not believers [compare French en — en honnête homme]; see WAG ii. § 56 a): namely

a. a primary predicate, Exod 18:4 the God of my fathers בְּעֶזְרִי‎ was my help, Psa 146:5; Hosea 13:9 (read בְעֶזְֶרךָ׃ מִי כִּי‎ with ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Che and others); Psa 68:5 שְׁמוֺ בְּיָהּ‎ his name consists in Yah, Job 23:13; 37:10. With the predicate in the plural (as plural of majesty) Psa 118:7 ׳י בְּעֹזְרָ֑י‎ J. is my great helper, 54:6 (see Che), Judg 11:35.

b. a secondary predicate, Exod 6:3 and I appeared unto them שַׁדָּ֑י בְּאֵל‎ as God Almighty, Num 26:53 בְּנַחֲלָה‎ as an inheritance, 34:2; Ezek 46:16; 47:14; Deut 10:22; 26:14 I have not put away therefrom בְּטָמֵא‎ as one unclean = while unclean, 28:62; Isa 40:10 יָבוֺא בְּחָזָק‎ he cometh as a strong one, Psa 35:2 (where see De) and rise up as my help, 35:16, 39:7; 55:19; Prov 3:26; Job 36:32 (De).

c. a predicate as accusative, Isa 48:10 I have refined thee בְכָ֑סֶף וְלֹא‎ but not as though silver, Ezek 20:41; Num 18:26; 36:2; Josh 13:6-7, 23:4; Ezek 45:1; 47:22 (twice in verse) (read יַמִּלוּ‎) 48:29 (see ᵐ5‎ Co) all בְּנַחֲלָה‎ (compare

b.), Psa 78:55 & allotted it נַחֲלָה בְּחֶבֶל‎ as a line of inheritance (i.e. as a measured inheritance). Isa 26:4 י עוֺלָמִים צוּר יהוה בְּיָהּ ׳כִּי‎ is different — for in Yah there is a rock of ages (compare Qor 4:7; 4:47 there is sufficiency in God as a patron).

d. in comparisons, Psa 37:20 consume away בֶּעָשָׁן‎ in the form of, as, smoke 78:33; 102:4; Job 34:36; 36:14.

II. Denoting proximity —

1 at, by (not very common): 1Sam 29:1 בָּעַיִן‎ by the spring; Ezek 10:15, 20 כְּבָר בִּנְהַר‎ by the river Chebar (1:3 עַל‎).

2 on: Gen 8:20; Num 23:2 בַּמִּזְבֵּחַ‎ on the altar; Judg 8:21 on the necks of the camels; 1Kin 2:5 and elsewhere בְּמָתְנָיו‎ on his loins; Isa 59:17 a helmet בְּראֹשׁוֺ‎ on his head.

3 often with verbs of touching, approaching, taking hold of, cleaving, etc., as תָּפַשׂ תָּמַךְ, מָּגַּע, קָרַב, נָגַשׁ, נָגַע, חָשַׁק, דָּבֵק, אָחַז,‎ (see these words).

4 with words expressing or implying an act of hostility —

a. against: Gen 16:12 בּוֺ כֹּל וְיַד בַכֹּל יָדוֺ‎ his hand against all, and the hand of all against him; מְּ יַד ׳הָֽיְתָה בּ‎ Deut 13:10; 1Sam 5:9; 18:17 +? verbs (q. v.) of fighting (רִיב נִלְחַם,‎), going up to invade (עָלָה‎), being angry (אַף חָרָה אָנַף, הִתְעַבֵּר,‎), sinning or acting treacherously (כִּחֵשׁ כִּזֵּב, שִׁקֵּר, מָּשַׁע, מָעַל, מָרָה, מָרַד, בָּגַד, חָטָא,‎), testifying (הֵעִיד עָנָה,‎), mocking (הֵתֵל הִלְעִיג,‎), feeling loathing (קוּץ‎), rebuking (גָּעַר‎: properly to protest loudly), speaking (דִּבֶּר‎: Num 12:8b), etc., & even (an extreme case) Hosea 7:14 בִי יָסוּרוּ‎ they turn aside (so as to be) against me. In a weaker sense בַּקִּיר מַשְׁתִּין‎ mingens ad parietem 1Sam 25:22 and elsewhere

b. down to, upon (super with accusative), especially in such phrases as בּוֺ דָּמָיו‎ Lev 20:9 and elsewhere his blood be upon him; בְראֹשׁוֺ דָּמוֺ‎ his blood be upon his head Josh 2:19; י (הֵשִׁיב בְּראֹשׁוֺ׳שׁוּב )‎ Judges 8:57 (רָעָה‎), 1Kin 2:33 (דָּם‎), 2:44 (רָעָה‎), Psa 7:17 (עֲמָלוֺ‎); מּ דֶּרֶךְ נָתַן ׳בְּראֹשׁוֺ‎ 1Kin 8:32 & often in Ezekiel, as Ezek 9:10; 11:21.

III. 1. With —

a. of accompaniment: Num 20:20 כָּבֵד בְּעַם‎ with much people, Josh 22:8; Judg 11:34; 1Kin 10:2; 2Kin 5:9; Jer 41:15; Exod 21:22 and he shall give בִּפְלִלִים‎ with arbitrators (arbitrators being employed), Isa 8:16 בְּלִמֻּדָֽי׃‎ with my disciples, i.e. having them present; Exod 8:1; 8:13; Jer 11:19 בְּלַחְמוֺ עֵץ‎ a tree with its sap; 1Kin 19:19 הֶעָשָׂר בִּשְׁנֵים וְהוּא‎ and he with the 12th.

b. often of what one takes or brings with one: Gen 32:11 בְּמַקְלִי‎ with my staff I passed over Jordan, Judg 11:34; 15:1; 1Sam 1:24; Isa 7:24; Micah 6:6 and elsewhere בְּ קִדֵּם‎ to go to meet with; בְּ בָּא‎ to come with Lev 16:3; Psa 66:13; 71:16. (In Arabic this usage is developed more fully than in Hebrew, and literally to come with, literally to go away with, are used idiomatically in the sense of to bring, and to take away respectively: WAG ii. § 56 b.) Hence בְּלֹא בִּבְלִי, בְּאֶפֶס, בְּאֵין,‎ = without.

c. of concomitant (or surrounding) conditions, as בְּחִמָּזוֺן‎ with (or in) haste; בְּצֶדֶק‎ with (or in) righteousness; בִּשְׁגָגָה‎ in error; שׁוֺפָר וּבְקוֺל בִּתְרוּעָה‎ 2Sam 6:15; often in such phrases as בְּצִדְקָֽתְךָ‎ Psa 31:2 in thy righteousness; בְּחַסְדְּךָ‎ in thy mercy Exod 15:13; — בְּאָשְׁרִי‎ with my happiness! = happy am I Gen 30:13; Psa 29:4 the voice of ׳י‎ is בַּכֹּחַ‎ with power = is powerful; Exod 32:12 בְּרָעָה‎ with evil purpose; Psa 73:8 בְרָע‎ in wickedness; 90:10 בִּגְבוּרֹת‎ with strength.

2 of the instrument or means: as

a. בַּחֶרֶב‎ with the sword Exod 5:3 etc.; בְּרַגְלַיִם‎ with the feet Isa 28:3; . . . בְּיַד‎ by the hand of ... (see below יָד‎); to stone בְּאֶבֶן‎ or בָּֽאֲבָנִים‎ with stones Lev 20:2; Num 14:10 etc.; בְּ שָׁתָה‎ to drink with a cup Gen 44:5; Amos 6:6 (compare in Aramaic Dan 5:2); to cry בְּגָרוֺן‎ with the throat Isa 58:1; to burn בָּאֵשׁ‎ in or with fire (often); to slay or to perish בָּרָעָב‎ through hunger or בַּדֶּבֶר‎ through pestilence Exod 16:3; Jer 21:9 + often (compare Job 27:15 יִקָּבֵ֑רוּ בַּמָּוֶת‎); to save with or by Judg 7:7; 1Sam 14:6.

b. idiomatic, with certain verbs, as בְּ שָׁחַק‎ to play with Job 40:29; בְּ עָבַד‎ to labour with a person (as with an instrument), i.e. to use him as a slave Exod 1:14; Jer 22:13; 27:7 and elsewhere; בְּ עָשָׂה‎ 18:23; Neh 9:24; Dan 11:7; Est 1:15; 2:11; 3:11; 6:6; & perhaps בְּ דִּבֶּר‎ (of God) to speak with one Num 12:2, 8a and elsewhere (see Ew§ 217 f. (3); DrSm ii. 23, 2). Further ביהוה הִתְנַבֵּא בַּבַּעַל,‎ to prophesy with or by ׳י‎ or Baal, ׳י‎ or Baal being the inspirer; דָּרַשׁ בְּ, שָׁאַל‎ to inquire or ask by means of a god (or oracle).

c. ביהוה‎ through ׳י‎ (= by His aid) in many connections, as Psa 18:30; 44:6; 56:5; 56:11; Psalm 60:14; Isa 26:13; 45:25; Hosea 1:7; Zech 10:12; with passive verbs Deut 33:29; Isa 45:17 (to be saved): and even of the immediate cause Num 36:2 to be commanded ביהוה‎ by ׳י‎, Gen 9:6 בָּאָדָם‎ by man shall his blood be shed (both unusual), Hosea 14:4.

d. allied is the use of בְּ‎ in such phrases as to bless, swear, speak, prophesy, etc., בְּשֵׁם‎ in the name of ... (i.e. the name being used or appealed to in the act) Deut 6:13; Jer 11:21, etc. (so to swear ביהוה‎ by ׳י‎ Josh 2:12 etc.,בִּימִינוֺ‎ Isa 62:8; to bless בְּךָ‎ with thee Gen 48:20, to swear with me Psa 102:9, i.e. using my name in oath, Jer 29:22); almost = in the authority and power of 1Sam 17:45; 25:5; 1Kin 21:8; Micah 4:5; Zech 10:12; Psa 20:6; 44:6; 89:25.

e. בַּמָּה‎ or בַּמֶּה‎ by means of what? how? Gen 15:8; Judg 6:15; 16:5-6, 10; 1Kin 22:21; Mal 2:17. בְּזֹאת‎ by means of this Gen 42:15, 33. Exod 7:17; Num 16:28; with this = on this condition Gen 34:15, 22; 1Sam 11:2; Isa 27:9.

3 of cost or price (the Beth pretii), the price, whether given or received, being treated as the instrumental means by which the act is accomplished, with, for, at the cost of: thus regularly

a. with שָׂכַר‎ hire Gen 30:16, מָּדָה‎ redeem Exod 34:20, אֵרֵשׂ‎ betroth 2Sam 3:14, קָנָה‎ buy 24:24; 1Kin 2:23 בְּנַפְשׁוֺ‎ at the cost of his life hath A. spoken this word, 2Sam 23:17 who went בְּנַפְשׂוֺתָם‎ at peril of their lives, Prov 7:23; Lam 5:9; Josh 6:26 יְיַסְּדֶנָּה בִּבְכֹרוֺ‎ at the price of his firstborn shall he lay its foundations, 1Chr 12:19 בְּרָאשֵׁינוּ‎ to the jeopardy of our heads he will fall away, etc.

b. with מָכַר‎ sell Deut 21:14; עָבַד‎ serve Gen 29:18, 20; Hosea 12:13; הֵמִיר‎ exchange Lev 27:10; Hosea 4:7 their glory I will exchange for ignominy, Psa 106:20; בְּנֶשֶׁךְ נָתַן‎ to give for interest Lev 25:37; Psa 15:5; in other connections Gen 23:9; 47:16f.; Isa 45:13; Lam 1:11; Cant 8:7; 8:11; Deut 19:21 בְּעַיִן עַיִן בְּנֶפֶשׁ נֶפֶשׁ‎ life for life, eye for eye; Isa 2:22 הוּא נֶחְשָׁב בַּמֶּה‎ at what is he to be accounted? 7:23 a thousand vines כָּ֑סֶף בְּאֶלֶף‎ at a thousand (shekels of) silver. — Hence (perhaps) the idiomatic usages בְשָׁנָה שָׁנָה‎ year for year, one year like another, annually Deut 15:20 and elsewhere; בְּיוֺם יוֺם‎ (late), בְּיוֺם כְּיוֺם‎ 1Sam 18:10; בְּפַעַם כְּפַעַם‎ (see מַּעַם יוֺם,‎); בְּחֹדֶשׁ חֹדֶשׁ‎ 1Chr 27:1.

4 rather peculiarly, in certain cases where the object of an action may be treated as the instrument by which it is accomplished: as בְּראֹשׁ הֵנַיעַ‎ to shake with the head Jer 18:6; Job 16:4 (as well as ראֹשׁ הֵנִיעַ‎ Psa 22:8); to open with the mouth Job 16:10, with the lips Psa 22:8; to gnash with the teeth Job 16:9 (to gnash the teeth Psa 35:16); to wink with the eye Prov 6:13 (to wink the eye, ib. 10:10); בְּקוֺל נָתַן‎ to utter with the voice Psa 46:7; 68:34; Jer 12:8 (but קוֺל נָתַן‎ is more common); to stretch out with the hand Lam 1:17; בַּמַּטֶּה הֵרִים‎ (unusual) Exod 7:20. So בְּשֵׁם קָרָא‎ to call with the name — in different senses, according to the context, namely, to proclaim 33:19; 34:5; Isa 44:5; Psa 49:12; to invoke Gen 4:26; 12:8; 1Kin 18:24-26 Isa 12:4; to name honourably 43:1; 45:3. compare Ew§ 282 d Ges§ 119. 3 b R. WAG ii. § 56 b β DeJob 31:12; Prov 20:30.

5 with a causal force, through, on account of: Gen 18:28 בַּחֲמִשָּׁה הֲתַשְׁחִית‎ wilt thou destroy on account of five the whole city? Lev 26:39; Num 16:26; Deut 9:4-5, 24:16 יוּמָֽתוּ׃ בְּחֶטְאוֺ אִישׁ‎ they shall be put to death, each because of his own sin (compare Jer 31:30; Ezek 3:18, see 18:17) 2Sam 3:27; 14:7 (compare Jonah 1:14) Isa 7:4 (|| מִן‎) 28:7 (|| מִן‎) 50:1; 53:5; 57:17; Jer 51:46; Psa 5:8; 5:11; 6:8 (|| מִן‎) 31:10; 32:3; 42:10; 90:9; 94:23. So in בִּגְלַל בַּאֲשֶׁר,‎ (see גָּלָל אֲשֶׁר,‎), & (sometimes) in בִּדְבַר‎ at, through, the word of ....

6 of the material with which a work is wrought, both absolute בַזָּהָב עָשָׁה‎ to work with gold Exod 31:4; 1Kin 7:14; and to make a thing with (in our idiom, of) gold Exod 38:8; Ezek 7:20; 1Kin 15:22 (בָּנָה‎). Without a verb Lev 13:52; 2Chr 9:18.

8 of a standard of measurement or computation, with, by: Exod 12:4 נְפָשֹׁת בְּמִכְסַת‎ by the computation of souls; Leviticus 5:25 and elsewhere בְּעֶרְכְּךָ‎ by thy reckoning; Ezek 4:10; בְּמִסְמָּר‎ by number Deut 25:2 +; . . . בְּמִסְמַּר‎ by the number of ... Lev 25:15, 50; Num 1:2, etc.; הַקֹּדֶשׁ בְּשֶׁקֶל‎ Exod 30:13 and elsewhere (in P); בָּאַמָּה‎ often (see אַמָּה‎); Deut 3:11 אִישׁ בְּאַמַּת‎ by the cubit of a man; 2Sam 14:26 הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּאֶבֶן‎. Of a model, Gen 1:26 בְּצַלְמֵנוּ‎ in our image, 5:1, 3; Exod 25:40; בְּדֶרֶךְ‎ with the way (= in the manner) of ... Isa 10:24, 26; Amos 4:10.

IV. בְּ‎ is used also with certain classes of verbs, though the explanation of its use may be sometimes doubtful: namely

a. with verbs of taking refuge, trusting, relying, as נִשְׁעַן חָסָה, בָּטַח, הֶאֱמִין,‎.

b. with verbs of ruling, governing, restraining, as שָׁלַט רָדָה, עָצַר, נָגַשׂ, מָשַׁל, מָלַךְ,‎.

c. with verbs of rejoicing, feeling pleasure or satisfaction, etc., as שָׂבַע רָצָה, חָפֵץ, שָׂמֵחַ, שׂוּשׂ, עָלַץ, גִּיל,‎ (but with this verb מִן‎ is more common). [Probably a case of

III. 5.]

d. with verbs expressive of sensible perception, to denote the pleasurable or attentive exercise of the faculty concerned, as בְּ שָׁמַע‎ to listen to, חָזָה רָאָה, בְּ, הִבִּיט‎, to look upon, בְּ הֵרִיחַ‎ to smell at (see these words).

e. occasionally also with verbs of speaking, thinking, mentioning, knowing, to denote the object of the action, as בְּ דִּבֶּר‎ to speak about Deut 6:7; Psa 87:3 and elsewhere (see below דִּבֶּר‎); שִׂיחַ הָגָה, בְּ, הִלֵּל‎ 44:9; 63:7; 69:13; יָדַע‎ Jer 38:24; זָכַר‎ once 3:16, הִזְכִּיר‎ often; Psa 71:6 תְהִלָּתִי בְּךָ‎ of thee is my praise.

V. Followed by an infinitive with, בְּ‎ forms a periphrasis for the gerund, though in English it is commonly to be rendered by a verb and conjunction, namely: —

1 as a temporal conjunction, as Gen 2:4 בְּהִבָּֽרְאָם‎ in their being created = when they were created, 4:8 בִּהְיוֺתָם‎ in their being (= when they were) in the field; and constantly. Sometimes it has in appearance the force of after that, as 33:18; Exod 3:12; 13:17; but as a rule this is really due to the action denoted by the infinitive being treated as extending over a period within which the action of the principal verb takes place: so especially in the phrase מִמִּצְרַיִם יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּצֵאת‎, even of events at the close of the 40 years, Deut 4:45; 23:5; Josh 5:4, the whole period being treated as that in which Egypt was left (compare 2Kin 2:1, where the time included is future). Cases, however, occur in which this explanation will hardly apply, as Deut 27:4; 24:12.

2 as a causal conjunction (compare above

III. 5), as Gen 19:16 עָלָיו י ׳בְּחֶמְלַת‎ through J.'s having compassion upon him, Exod 16:7; 33:16; 34:29; Deut 1:27 י ׳בְּשִׂנְאַת אֹתָנוּ‎ through J.'s hating us, etc. (9:28 similarly מִן‎), 1Kin 18:18 (= in that ye have ...) Ezek 9:8; 43:8; 44:7; 2Chr 28:6.

3 as a concessive conjunction, when = though: Isa 1:15; Psa 46:3 אָ֑רֶץ בְּהָמִיר‎ though the earth do change.

Note. — Exod 10:12 בָּאַרְבֶּה‎ can only be rendered 'with the locusts,' the locusts being conceived as implicit in Moses' uplifted hand: but probably לָאַרְבֶּה‎ should be read. Thrice in late Hebrew בְּ‎ is used peculiarly: 1Chr 7:23 for with misfortune was it in his house (בְּרָעָה‎ chosen for the purpose of explaining בְּרִיעָה‎); 9:33 בַּמְּלָאכָה עֲלֵיהֶם‎ it devolved upon them with the work; Ezra 3:3 for with terror (was it) upon them from the peoples of the countries (the sentence without a verb as often in Chronicles: DrIntr. 504 f.): compare 8:34. compare Ew§ 295 f.

2 (absolute) restrain, check (pain) i.e. assuage, so apparently ᵑ0‎ Job 16:5 (see Di Kau; I would not restrain condolence of my lips, ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Me, reading אחשׂך לא‎ for יחשׂך‎). — Ezek 30:18 see חשׁך‎.

Niph`al Imperfect יֵחָשֶׂךְרָֿע אֵיד לְיוֺם‎ Job 21:30 at the day of calamity the wicked is spared (passive of Qal 1 e); יֵחָשֵׂךְ‎ 16:6 be assuaged, of pain (pass of Qal 2).

חשכה.def:
H2825. chashekah

חֲשֵׁכָה‎ noun feminine darkness (chiefly in poetry) — ׳ח‎ Gen 15:12 2t., so read also probably Micah 3:6 (for חָֽשְׁכָה ᵑ0‎); חֲשֵׁיכָה‎ Psa 139:12; construct חֶשְׁכַּת‎ 18:12; plural חֲשֵׁכִים‎ Isa 50:10; — darkness, opposed to light (אוֺרָה‎) Psa 139:12; supernatural, ׳ח גדולה‎ Gen 15:12 (JE); מַיִם חֶשְׁכַּתֿ‎ Psa 18:12 in theoph. (but || 2Sam 22:12 חַשְׁרַתמֿים‎ a mass of water); figurative = lack of understanding Psa 82:5; = distress Isa 8:22 (|| צָרָה‎), 50:10.

חשל.def:
H2826. chashal

[חָשַׁל‎] verb shatter (Biblical Aramaic חֲשַׁל‎ shatter; Late Hebrew Pi`el, || משׁבר‎; Syriac forge a metal, Arabic drive cattle violently; Assyrian —ašâlu, shatter, destroy ZimBP 12 DlPr 42) —

Niph`al Participle figurative הַנֶּחֱשָׁלִים כָּלֿ‎ Deut 25:18 all the shattered ones, i.e. those broken down, worn out, followed by וְיָגֵעַ עָיֵף וְאַתָּה‎; others think = חלשׁ‎.

חשם.def:
H2366. Chuwshiym

I. חֻשִׁים חוּשִׁים,‎ proper name, feminine wife of Shaharaim of Benjamin, חוּשִׁים‎ 1Chr 8:8, חֻשִׁים‎ 8:11.

II. חֻשִׁים‎ proper name, masculine of Dan, ח דּן ׳וּבְנֵי‎ Gen 46:23 compareאַחֵר בְּנֵי חֻשִֿׁם‎ 1Chr 7:12 (see Be VB); = שׁוּחָם‎ (q. v.) Num 26:42 compare שׁוּחָתִי‎ 26:42; 26:43.

חשמון.def:
H2829. Cheshmon

חֶשְׁמוֺן‎ proper name, of a location town in southern Judah, site unknown Josh 15:27.

טַלְמֹן‎, once טַלְמוֺן‎ proper name, masculine name of porters.

1 1Chr 9:17; Ezra 2:42 = Neh 7:45.

2 Neh 11:19; 12:25 (טַלְמוֺן‎).

חשמל.def:
H2830. chashmal

חַשְׁמַל‎ noun [masculine] etymology and exact meaning dubious; evidently some shining substance; AV amber; supposed by Thes (q. v.) and most to be a brilliant amalgam of gold and silver, ᵐ5‎ ἤλεκτρον (see Liddell & Scott under the word

2), ᵑ9‎ electrum; see also Dl in BaerEzech. xii; only in the combination ח ׳כְּעֵין‎ like the appearance of ׳ח‎ Ezek 1:4, 27; הַחַשְׁמַ֑לָה בְּעֵין‎ 8:2 (on ending הָ֯‎ see Ges§ 90, 2 R a; Co strike out)

חשמנה.def:
H2832. Chashmonah

חַשְׁמֹנָה‎ proper name, of a location a station of Israel in wilderness Num 33:29-30, site unknown.

חשׁן‎ (√ of following; meaning not certain; Arabic is be excellent, beautiful; beauty, all excellence; hence possibly חשֶׁן‎ either as chief ornament of ephod, or as the most excellent, precious article of high priest's attire).

חשמנים.def:
the‎, He, fifth letter; = numeral 5 in post-Biblical Hebrew; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

הֶ הָ, הַ, , הַּ‎ (on the use of these different forms, see the Grammars: e.g. Ges§ 35),

definite article, the (so Moabite, Phoenician (Schröd§ 62-4), Liµyan (Northwest Arabia) ha (DHMEpigr. Denkm. 4. 13. 58 ff.); not Assyrian Aramaic or Ethiopic: Arabic , of which, before dentals, sibilants, and liquids, the l is written but not pronounced, thus pronounced 'ash-shamsu = Hebrew הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ‎) — in General the use of the article in Hebrew is analogous to its use in Greek or German: but naturally there are applications peculiar to Hebrew (compare with what follows Ges§ 126 Ew§ 277): —

1 joined with substantives:

a. to mark a definite concrete object, as Gen 1:1 the heavens and the earth, הַמֶּלֶךְ‎ the king, etc. Never, however (as in Greek e.g. ὁ Πλάτων), before true proper names, though it is used with certain terms, chiefly geographical, of which the original appellative sense has not been lost, as הַבַּעַל‎ 'Baal,' literally 'the lord,' in plural הַבְּעָלִים‎ i.e. the various local Baals, הַשָּׂטָן‎ the Adversary Job 1:6ff. (as a proper name שָׂטָן‎, 'Satan,' only 1Chr 21:1); הַלְּבָנוֺן‎ (but not הַחֶרְמוֺן‎), הַיַּרְדֵּן‎ (but not הָאַרְנֹן‎), הַשָּׁרוֺן הַכַּרְמֶל,‎ the Sharon, הַשְּׁפֵלָה‎ the (Judaean) lowland, הַמִּישׁוֺר הַכִּכָּר,‎ the (Moabite) table-land, הָעַי הָעֲרָבָה,‎ '`Ai,' הַגִּבְעָה‎ 'Gibeah,' Judg 20:5ff., הַגָּלִיל‎ 'Galilee,' הַגִּלְעָד הַבָּשָׁן, הַגִּלְבֹּעַ, הַגִּלְגָּל,‎ (often), הַמִּסְגָּה הָעֹפֶל, הַיְשִׁימוֺן, הָרָמָה, הַמִּצְמָּה, הַשִּׁטִּים,‎.

b. with an adjective to denote one who exhibits a quality κατ’ ἐξοχήν, i.e. to express the comparative or superlative degree: so often, as Gen 1:16 הגדל המאור‎ the greater light, הקטן המאור‎ the lesser light, 27:1 הגדול בנו‎ = his elder son, 48:14 הצעיר‎ the younger, 42:13 הַקָּטֹן‎ the little one, i.e. the youngest, (of Joseph's brethren), Lev 21:10 מֵאֶחָיו הַגָּדוֺל‎ the chiefest of his brethren, Num 35:25 + הגדול הכהן‎ the chief priest, ב ׳הצעיר‎ the least among Judg 6:15, מן הצעירה‎ the least of 1Sam 9:21, ב ׳הַיָּפָה‎ the fairest among Song 1:8; 2Kin 10:3; Prov 30:30, compare Job 14:15.

c. with nouns which are not definite in themselves, but acquire their definition from the context, or from the manner in which they are introduced: thus (α) in the standing phrases הַיּוֺם‎ to-day, Gen 4:14; 21:26 + often; הַלַּיְלָה‎ to-night, 19:5; 30:15 +, once 1Sam 15:16 last night; so הַשָּׁנָה‎ this year, 2Kin 19:29; Jer 28:16; הַמַּעַם‎ this time, Gen 18:32 +. (β) הַנָּהָר‎ the river (κατ’ ἐξοχήν), i.e. the Euphrates; Exod 2:15 the well, the well namely of the district, Josh 8:11 the valley, 1Sam 17:3; 19:10 the wall, 19:13 the bed, 20:21 הַנַּעַר‎ the lad (whom Jonathan would naturally take with him), 20:34 the table. Hence occas. where a suffix would define the noun more precisely, as הַחֲמוֺר‎ 2Sam 19:27 + = my ass, Judg 3:20; 1Sam 1:9 הַכִּסֵּא‎ = his seat, Judg 4:15; 1Kin 22:35; 2Kin 10:15 + הַמֶּרְכָּבָה‎, 1Sam 18:10; 20:33 הַחֲנִית‎.

d. it is a peculiarity of Hebrew thought to conceive an object as defined by its being taken for a particular purpose, and thus by a kind of prolepsis to prefix the article to the noun denoting it: 1Sam 10:1 and Samuel took הַשֶּׁמֶן אֶתמַּֿךְ‎ literally the cruse of oil, not, however, a cruse which had been defined previously, but one rendered definiteby being now taken; in English idiom 'a cruse of oil,' 10:25 בַּסֵּפֶר‎ literally in the scroll or book, the one, namely taken for the purpose, i.e. in a scroll (so Exod 17:14; Num 5:23; Job 19:23), 21:10 בַּשִּׂמְלָה‎, Judg 4:18 בַּשְּׂמִיכָה וַתְּכַסֵּהוּ‎, 4:19; 7:13 הָאֹהֶל‎ a tent, 8:25; 9:48 אֶתהַֿקַּרְדֻּמֹּת‎ hatchets, 20:16 every one able to sling אֶלהַֿשַּׂעֲרָה בָּאֶבֶן‎ with a stone at a hair, 1Sam 6:8 בָּאַרְגָּז‎ (unless indeed the אַרְגָּז‎ was an understood appendage in every cart), Num 11:27 הַנַּעַר‎, a young man, 13:23 בַּמּוֺט‎ on a pole, Josh 2:15 בַּחֶבֶל‎ with a cord, 2Sam 17:17 השׁפחה‎ a girl (compare Dr1Sam 1:4; 19:13). Sometimes it is uncertain whether an article is to be referred to c or

d: e.g. 1Sam 2:13 his prong or a prong, 2Sam 18:9 his mule or a mule, etc.

e. with nouns that denote objects or classes of objects that are known to all, as הַמַּיִם הַזָּהָב, הַצּאֹן,‎; Gen 13:2 Abram was very rich וּבַזָּהָב בַּכֶּסֶף בַּמִּקְנֶה‎, Exod 31:4 וּבַכֶּסֶף בַּזָּהָב לַעֲשׂוֺת‎, Deut 14:26 and thou shalt lay out the money וּבַשֵּׁכָר וּבַיַּיִן וּבַצּאֹן בַּבָּקָר‎, 2Kin 9:30 עֵינֶיהָ בַּמּוּךְ וַתָּשֶׂם‎, in French 'elle mit du fard à ses yeux.' It is, however, remarkable that this usage depends mostly on the punctuation, הַלֶּחֶם הַיַּיִן, הַכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. (except as applied to denote definite quantities of gold, wine, etc., as Josh 6:24) being far less common than יַיִן כֶּסֶף,‎ etc., but לַכֶּסֶף בַּכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. being much more frequently than לְכֶסֶף בְּכֶסֶף,‎ etc.: for instances in which the article forms part of the consonantal text, see Gen 6:20; 7:8 + העוף‎ and הבהמה‎, Deut 8:3 הַלָּחֶם‎, 1Kin 5:8; 5:13; Isa 28:7 הַיַּיִן‎ and הַשֵּׁכָר‎, 60:17; Ezek 15:4, 7 הָאֵשׁ‎, Hab 2:5; Prov 20:1; Psalm 65:14 הַצּאֹן‎, Song 1:11; Eccl 7:12. compare below,

f. in comparisons, the object compared being, as a rule, not an individual as such, but one exhibiting the characteristics of a class: Isa 1:18 כַּתּוֺלָע כַּשָּׁנִים,‎ like scarlet, like crimson (both meant Generally), 5:24 יִהְיֶה כַּמַּק‎, 5:28 כַּצַּר‎ and כַּסּוּפָה‎, 10:14 כַּקֵּן‎, 13:8 כַּיּוֺלֵדָה‎ (as always with this word, e.g. 42:14; Psa 48:7), 11:7 כַּבָּקָר‎; + often (The usage is not, however, quite uniform, at least according to the punctuation: there occurs e.g. כְּקַשׁ‎ Job 41:21; Isa 47:14; כְּאַרְיֵה‎ Psa 7:3 and elsewhere: and we find both כַּלָּבִיא‎) Isa 5:29 and כְּלָבִיא‎ Hosea 13:8; כָּאֲרִי‎ Isa 38:13 and כַּאֲרִי‎ Num 24:9; כַּגִּבּוֺר‎ Isa 42:13 and כְּגבור‎ Job 16:14; etc.) Similarly Gen 19:28 הַכִּבְשָׁן כְּקִיטֹר‎ as the smoke of a furnace, Num 11:8, 12 אֶתהַֿיֹּנֵק הָאֹמֵן יִשָּׂא כַּאֲשֶׁר‎, Deut 28:29 (הָעִוֵּר‎), Judg 8:18b הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּנֵי כְּתֹאַר‎, 14:6 הַגְּדִי כְּשַׁסַּע‎ like (a lion's) rending a kid, 16:9; 1Kin 14:15; Zech 12:10 הַיָּחִיד עַל מִסְמֵּד כְּ‎ as mourning over an only child, 13:9 +. Where, however, the standard of comparison is not the class in General, but only a particular part of it, defined by a special epithet (whether adjective or verb), the article is naturally omitted: thus כַּמֹּץ‎ like chaff (in General) Isa 41:15, but עֹבֵר כְּמֹץ‎ like chaff passing away 29:5; כַּצֵּל‎ Job 14:2, but נָטוּי כְּצֵל‎ Psa 102:12; כַּקַּשׁ‎ Isa 40:24, but נִדָּף כְּקַשׁ‎ 41:2; כָּאַיָּל‎ 35:6, but, וג על תַּעֲרֹג ׳כְּאַיָּל‎ like a hind (that) longeth for streams of water Psa 42:2; כָּאֵשׁ‎ Isa 9:17, but יער תבער כְּאֵשׁ‎ like fire (that) kindleth a wood Psa 83:15; כֶעָשָׁן‎ Isa 51:6, but מֵאֲרֻבָּה כְּעָשָׁן‎ like smoke from a chimney Hosea 13:3: so Isa 62:1b Job 9:26; 11:16 עָֽבְרוּ כְּמַיִם‎ like waters (that) have passed by, etc.; Deut 32:2 a כַּטַּל כַּמָּטָר,‎, but 32:2 b עֲלֵיעֵֿשֶׂב כִּרְבִיבִים עֲלֵידֶֿשֶׁא, כִּשְׂעִירִים‎. Where the article is found, although a rel. clause follows (as Psa 1:4; 49:13; Isa 61:10), this is probably to be regarded not as limiting the class of object compared, but as describing it.

g. prefixed to generic nouns (in the singular) it designates the class, i.e. it imparts to the noun a collective force, as Exod 1:22 כָּלהַֿבֵּן‎ all (literally the whole of) the sons, כָּלהַֿבַּת‎ all the daughters, Lev 17:8, 10 מִןהַֿגֵּר‎ of the strangers, who sojourn in their midst, Num 21:7 הַגנָּחָשׁ‎ the serpents; Gen 14:13; Ezek 24:26; 33:21 הַמָּלִיט‎ those who escaped; Josh 6:7 + הֶחָלוּץ‎, v 9:13 הַמְאַסֵּף‎; 8:19 הָאוֺרֵב‎; 1Sam 13:17 הַמַּשְׁחִית‎; Micah 2:13; Isa 6:4 הַקּוֺרֵא‎ the choir of criers; 1Sam 24:14 הַקַּדְמֹנִי‎ the ancients; Eccl 7:26 אֶתהַֿאִשָּׁה‎ woman, and often with Gentile names, as הַיְבוּסִי‎ the Jebusites, וְהַמְּלֵתִי הַכְּרֵתִי‎ 2Sam 8:18 and elsewhere, הַדָּנִי‎ Judg 18:1 etc., הַלֵּוִי‎ the Levites, Num 3:20, 18:23; Mal 2:8; Psa 135:20 +.

h. with nouns denoting abstract ideas, especially the names of moral qualities (compare Greek ἡ δίκη, French la justice), chiefly in two cases — (α) where the article is recognizable in the consonantal text, exceptionally, when some emphasis or definiteness is intended, as Deut 7:9 והחסד הברית שׁומר‎; הזה החסד‎ 2Sam 2:5; 1Kin 3:6; והרחמים החסד את‎ Jer 16:5 (contr. Zech 7:9); הצדק‎ Isa 1:26; 61:3; Eccl 3:16; הַצְּדָקָה‎ Isa 32:17 (twice in verse) (contrast 32:16) Dan 9:7 (emphatic); הַדַּעַת‎ Hosea 4:6; הָאֱמֶת‎ Gen 32:11 (followed by אֲשֶׁר‎), Isa 59:15 (contrast 59:14) Zech 8:3, 19; הָאֱמוּנָה‎ Isa 11:5b (contr. va) Jer 7:28; הַחָכְמָה‎ Job 28:12, 20; הַחַיִּים‎ Gen 2:9 +; הָאַהֲבָה‎ Song 2:7; 3:5; 8:4, 7; הַשֶּׁקֶר‎ Jer 7:4, 8; 23:26; הַמָּוֶת‎ Isa 25:8; Ruth 1:17 +; הָרֶשַׁע‎ Psa 125:3; Eccl 3:16; הָרִשְׁעָה‎ Zech 5:8; הַחשֶׁךְ‎ Isa 60:2; Eccl 2:13; see also Deut 30:15, 19 (Jer 21:8), 1Kin 7:14; Jer 32:19; Mal 2:5 והשׁלום החיים‎, Psa 123:4; 130:4; Dan 9:9; 1Chr 29:11; 2Chr 1:12; Prov 31:30; Eccl 2:18, 17; 7:12, 19; 10:6; 11:10: but in all such cases אֱמֶת צֶדֶק, חֶסֶד,‎, etc. are far more common. (β) where the article depends on the punctuation, after prepositions, especially בְּ‎, but with much irregularity, as בַּחֶסֶד‎ Isa 16:5; Prov 20:28 (but ׳בְּח‎ Hosea 2:21; Prov 16:6), בַּצֶּדֶק‎ 25:5 (elsewhere always ׃בְּצ ׳בִּצְדָקָה‎ also always); בֶּאֱמֶת‎ and בֶּאֱמוּנָה‎ always; בַּשֶּׁקֶר‎ Isa 28:15 (but || כָּזָב‎, not הַכָּזָב‎) Jer 5:31; 13:25; 20:6; 23:14 (בְּשֶׁקֶר‎ 3:10; 29:9); בַּשָּׁלוֺם‎ Psa 29:11; Job 15:21 (elsewhere בְּשָׁלוֺם‎); Zech 12:4 to smite וּבַעִוָּרוֺן בַּשִּׁגָּעוֺן‎ (but Deut 28:28 וּבְעורון בְּשׁגעון‎), compare Gen 19:11; Deut 28:22; to enter with one בַּמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Job 9:32; 22:4 (but בְּמשׁפט‎ Psa 143:2), contrast also Prov 18:5; with 24:23; לַמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Isa 59:11; Psa 9:8 (but ׳לְמ‎ Isa 5:7; Psa 122:5); Prov 2:2; 7:4 לַחָכְמָה‎, (but never הַחכמה‎ in Proverbs 1-9, or indeed in the whole book); 2:3; 7:4 לַבִּינָה‎, Job 39:17 בַּבִּינָה‎ (but never הַבִּינָה‎); Prov 2:2-3,לַתְּבוּנָה‎ (but הַתְּבוּנָה‎ only 1Kin 7:14 emphatic); to perish בַּצָּמָא‎ Judg 15:18 +; Isa 29:21 בַּתֹּהוּ‎, 32:19 הָעִיר תִּשְׁמַּל בַּשִּׁמְּלָה‎ German in die Niedrigkeit sinkt die Stadt, 45:16 together they go בַכְּלִמָּה‎ (in die Schmach), 46:2 בַּשְּׁבִי‎ into captivity, 47:5 בַחשֶׁךְ בֹּאִי‎ (so always: never בְחשׁך‎). The living language may have used the article more readily after a preposition, where it did not lengthen the word by an entire syll.; still the disparity of usage between α and β makes it not improbable that the article in β is in many cases not original but due to the punctuators.

i. to mark the vocative: 1Sam 17:55 הַמֶּלֶךְ חֵינֿפשׁך‎ as thy soul liveth, O king, I do not know, 17:58 הַנַּעַר אתה מי בן‎ Whose son art thou, lad ? 2Sam 14:4 Help, O king ! 1Kin 18:26 עֲנֵנוּ הַבַּעַל‎, 2Kin 9:5 הַשָּׂר אֵלֶיךָ‎, Isa 42:18 שְׁמָ֑עוּ הֵַחרְשִׁים‎, Jer 2:31 וג רְאוּ אַתֶּם ׳הַדּֿוֺר‎, Ezek 37:4 הַיְּבֵשׁוֺת הָעֲצָמוֺת‎ O dry bones, Mal 3:9 כֻּלּוֺ הַגּוֺי‎ (Dr§ 198 Obs. 2).

N.B. In poetry, the article is frequently dispensed with before words which would naturally take it in prose: thus Psa 2:2; 2:8; 2:10 & often אֶרֶץ‎; 8:9; 18:10; 33:6 + שָׁמַיִם‎; (rarely in prose, Gen 1:8; 2:4; 1Kin 8:35); 21:2; 1Ki 45:14; 1Ki 45:16; 1Ki 61:7 and elsewhere מֶלֶךְ‎; 1Ki 66:6; 1Ki 72:8 + יָם‎; 1Ki 59:7; 1Ki 59:15 עִיר‎; Judg 5:2; Psa 18:44 עָם‎ etc.; 9:6; 9:17 & often רָשָׁע‎; Isa 1:2, 6, 21; 3:10-11, 11:6-7, 8.

2 With adjectives, participles, and demonstrative pronouns (אלה זאת, זה, הם, המה, היא, הוא,‎): namely

a. (so regularly) when the substantive qualified by these words is defined by it likewise, as הגדול המלך‎ = ὁ βασιλεὺς ὁ μέγας, Gen 2:12 ההוא הארץ‎, 20:1 הַזֶּה הַדָּבָר‎, Josh 2:3 אליך הבאים האנשׁים‎ = οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς σέ, Gen 13:5; 16:13; 24:65; 32:21; Judg 6:28; Isa 65:3-4, 5; 66:24; Psa 31:9. So also with adjectives & participles, if the substantive be defined by a suffix (as Deut 4:37 הַגָּדֹל בְּכֹחוֺ‎, 1Sam 8:14 הַטֹּבוֺת זֵיתֵיכֶם‎); and with a pronoun, if it be defined by a Genitive (as Deut 29:20; 1Sam 14:29; 15:14; 2Kin 6:32 הַזֶּה בֶןהַֿמְּרַצֵּחַ‎ this son of a murderer), but not if it be defined by a suffix, as Exod 10:1 אֵלֶּה אֹתֹתַי‎ (not הָאֵלָּה אתתי‎), Josh 2:14 זֶה דְבָרֵנוּ‎ this our word (not ׳ד הַזֶּה‎): see Dr§ 209 Obs. Similarly when the article with the participle has a resumptive force, Psa 33:15 (Psalm 14, he looketh forth from the place, &c.), לִבָּם יַחַד הַיֹּצֵר‎ he that formeth, etc., 19:11 מִזָּהָב הַנֶּחֱמָדִים‎ which (Psalm 10 b) are more desirable than gold, 49:7. (:6 b the iniquity of my aggressors surroundeth me), הַבֹּטְחִים‎ who trust in their riches, etc., Gen 49:21; Isa 46:6; 51:20; Job 6:16 + (see Dr§ 135. 7).

b. (rare) when the substantive qualified by the adjective or participle was felt to be sufficiently definite for its own article to be dispensed with, as sometimes with the word day Gen 1:31 השׁשׁי יום‎, 2:3 השׁביעי יום‎, Exod 12:15, 18; 20:10 (= Deut 5:14) Lev 19:6; 22:27: so with מָנוֺא‎ entrance Jer 38:14, שַׁעַר‎ Zech 14:10; חָצֵר‎ court 1Kin 7:8, 12; Ezek 40:28 and elsewhere; also in certain phrases (peculiar to P) where the substantive is defined by כל‎, as Gen 1:21 הַחַיָּה כָּלנֶֿפֶשׁ‎ all living souls, 1:28 הָרֹמֶשֶׂת כָּלחַֿיָּה‎ all living things that creep, etc., 7:21; 9:10; Lev 11:10, 46; further in isolated cases, hardly reducible to rule, 24:10; 1Sam 12:23 הַטּוֺבָה דֶּרֶךְ‎, 16:23 הָרָעָה רוּחַ‎, 2Sam 12:4 העשׁיר לְאישׁ‎ Jer 6:20; 17:2; Zech 4:7; Psa 104:18; Ezra 10:9 הַתְּשִׁיעִי חֹדֶשׁ‎ (quite exceptional in OT). (With pronouns this use is so rare that, where it occurs, it is dubious if the text be sound: 1Sam 17:12, 17; Jer 40:3 Kt Micah 7:11). And with the participle: 1Sam 25:10 הַמִּתְמָּֽרְצִים עֲבָדִים רַבִּים‎ many are the slaves who break away etc., Isa 7:20; Jer 27:3; 46:16 = 50:16 הַיּוֺנָה חֶרֶב‎ the oppressing sword, Ezek 2:3 (but ᵐ5‎ Co omit הגוים‎), 14:22; 32:22, 24; Psa 62:4; Prov 26:18; Judg 21:19 (very anomalous, read probably לַמְּסִלָּה‎). This usage is somewhat more frequently in the later parts of OT; and in Post-Biblical Hebrew it is very General (e.g. הָרַע יֵצֶד‎ the evil inclination): see further Dr§ 209.

c. with the participle, where the participle with the article forms really the subject: Gen 2:11 הַסּוֺבֵב הוּא‎ not 'it was encompassing,' but 'it is that which encompassed,' 45:12 הַמְדַבֵּר מִּי‎ my mouth is that which speaketh, Deut 3:21 הָראֹוֺת עֵינֶיךָ‎ thine eyes were those which saw, 4:3; 8:18 ὅτι οὗτος ἐστιν ὁ διδοὺς σοί, Isa 14:27; 66:9 (see Dr§ 135. 7).

3 The article is prefixed exceptionally — mostly in the latest Hebrew — with the force of a relative to the verb: Josh 10:24 אִתּוֺ הֶהָֽלְכוּא‎ that went with him, Ezek 26:17, הַהֻ֫לָּלָה הָעִיר‎, 1Chr 26:28 שְׁמוּאֵל הַהִקְדִּישׁ וְכֹל‎ and all that Samuel had dedicated, 29:8, 17; 2Chr 1:4 ַבּהֵכִין‎ in (the place) that he had prepared, 29:36; Ezra 8:25; 10:14, 17. According to the punctuation, it occurs similarly elsewhere, as Gen 18:21 הַשָבּאָה‎ (so 46:27; Job 2:11), 21:3 הַנּוֺלַדלֿוֺ‎, 1Kin 11:9 & Dan 8:1 הַנִּרְאָה‎, Isa 51:10 הַשָּׂ֨מָה֨‎, 56:3 הַנִּלְוָה‎, Ruth 1:22; 2:6; 4:3 (all הַשָּׁ֫בָה‎): but in all these passages, the change of a point, or even sometimes of an accent, would restore the normal participial construction (as לוֺ הַנּוֺלָד הַבָּשָאה,‎ compare Gen 48:5, הַנִּרְאֶה‎), which is, no doubt, what was intended by the original writers, and is recognised elsewhere by the Masora, e.g. 12:7; 35:1 הַנִּרְאֶה‎, 46:26 & Ruth 4:11 הַבָּאָ֣ה‎ (compare Ew§ 331 b Ges138, 3 b). Once, still more anomalously, before a preposition 1Sam 9:24 וְהֶעָלֶיהָ‎ (as though καὶ τὸ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς): but read probably וְהָאַלְיָה‎ and the fat tail, see Dr. (In Arabic also occurs, though very rarely, as a relative: WAG i. § CG 117). — On the anomalous use of the article with a word in the stative construct, see Grammars, as Ew§ 290 d, Ges§ 127 R. 4, also Dr§ 190-1.

חשן.def:
H2833. choshen

ח֫שֶׁן‎ noun masculine the breast-piece or sacred pouch, containing the ותמים אורים‎, worn on the breast of the high priest when he ministered in the Holy Place to bring the tribes for memorial. before ׳י‎. It was made of the same material as the ephod (see אֵפוֺד‎), a span square; set in front with twelve jewels in four rows, engraved with the names of the twelve tribes. It was firmly fastened to the shoulders of the ephod by gold chains passing through gold rings, and to the lower part of the ephod just above the girdle by a blue ribbon passing through other gold rings. It was (ה)מִשְׁמָּט חשֶׁן‎ ( Exod 28:15, 29, 30) pouch of judgment, because of the decision given by the וְתֻמִּים אוּרִים‎. The name occurs only in P, 25:7; 28:4, 15, 22, 23 (twice in verse); 28:24, 26, 28 (twice in verse); 28:29-30, 29:5; 35:9, 27; 39:8-9, 15, 16, 17, 19, 21 (twice in verse); Lev 8:8 (twice in verse). — See NowArchaeology ii. 119.

חשק.def:
H2837. chesheq

חֵ֫שֶׁק‎ noun masculine desire = thing desired — construct שְׁלֹמֹה חֵשֶׁק‎ 1Kin 9:19 2Chr 8:6; 1Kin 9:1; suffix חִשְׁקִי נֶשֶׁף‎ Isa 21:4 the twilight of my pleasure .

H2840. chishshur

[חִשּׁוּר‎] noun [masculine] nave, hub of a wheel (which gather in the spokes) — plural suffix חִשֻּׁרֵיהֶם‎ 1Kin 7:33.

חשׁשׁ‎ (√ of following; compare Arabic hasten, hurry (transitive), particles of straw, sand, dust, as flying quickly about; see LagBN 40).

[חַשְׁרָה‎] noun feminine collection, mass, only (si vera 1.) חַשְׁרַתמַֿיִם‎ 2Sam 22:12 (חֶשְׁכַּת‎ in || Psa 18:12).

חשש.def:
H2842. chashash

חֲשַׁשׁ‎ noun masculine Isaiah 59:24 chaff; — absolute קַשׁ ח ׳תַּהֲרוּ תֵלְדוּ‎ Isa 33:11 ye conceive chaff, ye bring forth stubble (figurative of vain attempt of Assyr.); construct יִרְמֶּה ׳ח לֶהָבָה‎ 5:24 (|| קַשׁ‎) as flaming chaff sinketh down (simile of perishing of heedless Judahites).

חֻשָׁתִי‎ see חושׁ‎.

חִתָּה חַת,‎ see חתת‎.

1 of individual, with article׳הַח‎ 2Sam 21:18 = 1Chr 20:4; 2Sam 23:27 = 1Chr 11:29, see also 27:11.

H2817. Chasupha

חֲשֻׁפָא חֲשׂוּפָא,‎ proper name, masculine head of a family of Nethinim among the returning exiles חֲשׂוּפָא‎ Ezra 2:43 = חֲשֻׂפָא‎ Neh 7:46.

חשופי.def:
H2834. chasaph

חָשַׂף‎ verb strip off, strip, make bare —

Qal Perfect חָשַׂף‎ Isa 52:10, חֲשָׂפָהּ‎ Joel 1:7, חָשַׂפְתִּי‎ Jer 13:26; 49:10; Imperfect וַיֶּחֱשׂף‎ Psa 29:9; Imperative feminine singular חֶשְׂמִּיֿ‎ Isa 47:2; Infinitive absolute חָשׂף‎ Joel 1:7; construct לַחְשׂף‎ Isa 30:14; Hag 2:16; Passive participle חֲשׂוּפָה‎ Ezek 4:7, חֲשׂוּפַי‎ Isa 20:4 (plural construct ? compare below). —

1 strip off, expose oneself by removing (object שֹׁבֶל‎, flowing skirt, train) Isa 47:2 of Babylon, personified as queen (|| שׁוֺק גַּלִּי‎), ׳ח עַלמָּֿנַיִךְ שׁוּלַיִךְ‎ Jer 13:26.

2 strip, lay bare, figurative of ׳י‎ Isa 52:10 object קדשׁו זְרוֺעַ‎; of prophet, Ezek 4:7 (but Co strike out see as interpolation); object person Jer 49:10 (|| גִּלֵּיתִי‎); חשׂפהּ חָשׂף‎ Joel 1:7 of locusts stripping fig-tree; שֵׁת חֲשׂוּפַי‎ Isa 20:4 (participle either singular collective, with formative ending יַ֯‎, De LagSe i. 19 (compare 69), BN 192; or plural construct, see Ges§ 87, 1 c.); ׳ח יְעָרוֺת‎ Psa 29:9 of voice of ׳י‎ (i.e. a storm) stripping forests.

3 draw (water) Isa 30:14; (wine) Hag 2:16; properly take from the surface, skim.

חֲשׂוּפַי‎ Isa 20:4 see חשׂף‎. above

Qal Perfect חָשַׂף‎ Isa 52:10, חֲשָׂפָהּ‎ Joel 1:7, חָשַׂפְתִּי‎ Jer 13:26; 49:10; Imperfect וַיֶּחֱשׂף‎ Psa 29:9; Imperative feminine singular חֶשְׂמִּיֿ‎ Isa 47:2; Infinitive absolute חָשׂף‎ Joel 1:7; construct לַחְשׂף‎ Isa 30:14; Hag 2:16; Passive participle חֲשׂוּפָה‎ Ezek 4:7, חֲשׂוּפַי‎ Isa 20:4 (plural construct ? compare below). —

חת.def:
H2845. Cheth

חֵת‎ proper name, masculine apparently represented as ancestor of the Hittites (etymology and meaning unknown; pronounced as from √ עע֞‎ in Hebrew & Assyrian, but not Egyptian; see חִתִּי‎ below) — 'begotten' by Canaan Gen 10:15 (J) = 1Chr 1:13; elsewhere only in combination with בְּנוֺת בְּנֵי,‎;

a. בְּנֵיחֵֿת‎ according to P lived at Mamre (Hebron), and one of them sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah for a sepulchre Gen 23:3, 5, 10 (twice in verse); 23:16, 18, 20; 25:10; 49:32.

b. בְּנוֺת(ֿ)חֵת‎ only of wives of Esau Gen 27:46 (twice in verse) (P; ᵐ5‎ omits vb; || הָאָרֶץ בְּנוֺת‎ = כְּנָ֑עַן בְּנוֺת‎ 28:1).

חתה.def:
H2846. chathah

[חָתָה‎] verb snatch up, usually fire, coals (Late Hebrew id.; חֲתָא ᵑ7‎, id. (rare); Assyrian —atû is destroy (i.e. snatch away ?) see SASmAsrb i. 90) —

Qal Imperfect יַחְתֶּה‎ Prov 6:27; suffix יַחְתְּךָ‎ Psa 52:7; Infinitive construct לַחְתּוֺת‎ Isa 30:14; Participle חֹתֶה‎ Prov 25:22; — snatch up, with accusative מִיָּקוּד אֵשׁ‎ Isa 30:14 to snatch up fire from a hearth (|| מִגֶּבֶא מים לַחְשׂף‎); בְּחֵיקוֺ אֵשׁ‎ Prov 6:27 shall a man snatch up fire in his bosom and his garments not be burned ? (in simile of adulterer); pregnantly seize (and put) upon ח אַתָּה ׳גְּחָלִים עלרֿאֹשׁוֺ‎ 25:22; מֵאֹ֑הֶל וְיִסָּֽחֲךָ יַחְתְּךָ‎ Psa 52:7 God . . . shall snatch thee away, and pluck thee up tent-less.

חתול.def:
H2848. chittul

חִתּוּל‎ noun [masculine] bandage — ׳ח‎ Ezek 30:21, for broken arm (in figurative of Pharaoh's broken arm).

חתחתים.def:
H2849. chathchath

[חַתְחַת‎] noun [masculine] terror, only plural בַּדֶּרֶךְ חַתְחַתִּים‎ Eccl 12:5 terrors are in the way (|| ירא‎).

חתי.def:
H2850. Chitti

חִתִּי‎ adjective and

name, of a people Hittite(s) (Egyptian –-tá, –etá W Max MüllAsien u. Europa, 319 ff.; Assyrian –atti, SchrKG 192 ff. COT on Gen 10:19 DlPa, 269 ff.; Tel el-Amarna –atti, –atta BezTel el Amarn. Brit. Mus. 150) — masculine always with article הַחִתִּי‎ 23:10; Exod 3:8 +; feminine חִתִּית‎ Ezek 16:3, 45; masculine plural הַחִתִּים‎ Josh 1:4 3t.; feminine plural חִתִּיֹּת‎ 1Kin 11:1; —

1. adjective , of seller of Machpelah to Abraham, הַחִתִּי עֶפְרוֺן‎ Gen 23:10; 49:29-30, 50:13; ׳הַח בֶּןצֹֿחַר עֶפְרֹן‎ 25:9 (all P); of fathers of Esau's wives ׳הַח בְּאֵרִי‎ 26:34; הַח ׳אֵילוֺן‎ 26:34; 36:2 (all P); also of warriors of David, הַח ׳אֲחִימֶלֶךְ‎ 1Sam 26:6, and especially הַח ׳אוּרִיָּה‎ 2Sam 11:3, 6, 17, 21, 24; 12:9-10, 23:39; 1Kin 15:5; 1Chr 11:41; feminine singular = substantive, only of (religious) ancestry of Jerusalem Ezek 16:3 thy father was the Amorite, and thy mother was a Hittite woman חִתִּית‎, similarly 16:45; feminine plural = substantive of Solomon's foreign wives, חִתִּיֹּת‎ 1Kin 11:1 Hittite women (+ צֵדְנִיֹּת אֲדֹמִיֹּת, עַמּוֺנִיּוֺת, מוֺאֲבִיּוֺת,‎).

2. n. usually

a. collective הַחִתִּי‎ the Hittites: in lists of Canaanitish peoples Gen 15:20 (JE), Exod 3:8, 11 (both J), 13:5; 23:23, 28; 33:2; 34:11; Num 13:29; Josh 3:10 (all J E), Deut 7:1; 20:17; Josh 9:1; 12:8; 24:11 (all D); read also for הַחִוִּי‎ Judg 3:3 (so We Mey BuUrg 350); in Josh 11:3 (D) strike out הַחִתִּי‎ We Mey Bul.c., and read then הַחִתִּי‎ for הַחִוִּי‎ vb (so ᵐ5‎, not ᵐ5‎L); further 1Kin 9:20 2Chr 8:7; Ezra 9:1; Neh 9:8.

b. plural הַחִתִּים אֶרֶץ כֹּל ׃הַחִתִּים‎ Josh 1:4 (D) nearly = land of Canaanites; הַח ׳ארץ‎ specifically of northern home of Hittites Judg 1:26; so also 2Sam 24:6 where read קֵ֫דְשָׁה הַחִתִּים אֶרֶץ‎ (for חָדְשִׁי תחתים ᵑ0‎, see קֵדֶשׁ חָדְשִׁי,‎); הַחִתִּים מַלְכֵי‎ 1Kin 10:29 2Chr 1:17 (both + אֲרָם מַלְכֵי‎), 2Kin 7:6 (+ מִצְרַיִם מַלְכֵי‎, both feared by אֲרָם‎). Hence it appears that (םׅ הַחִתִּי‎ had their proper seat in the north — where also they were encountered by Assyrians from time of Tiglath-Pileser I (see Schr Dl1. c.), and by Egyptians from time of Tutmes III (see W Max Müll.l.c.) — (compare also Judg 3:3; Josh 11:3 above), but that individual Hittites were known in Israel (compare, besides 1Sam 2:6; 2Sam 11:3 etc., 1Kin 9:20 above); that the Hittites were regarded (by J E D) as one of the peoples of Canaan, and that the name even came to be used in more General sense for Canaanites. Only in P do they appear as having a definite settlement in the south, and are designated by בְּנֵיחֵֿת‎ (see חֵת‎), as well as by the adjective הַחִתִּי‎.

חתית.def:
H2851. chittith

חִתִּית‎ noun feminine terror, only Ezekiel; absolute ׳ח‎ Ezek 32:23, but Co reads חִתִּיתָם‎ (with ᵐ5‎ and 32:24; 32:26); construct id. 32:27; suffix חתיתו‎ 32:32 Kt (> חִתִּיתִי‎ Qr); חִתִּיתָם‎ 32:24 2t.+ 26:17 (read חִתִּיתָהּ‎, with ᵐ5‎ Ew Co, see VB), 32:30 (read חַתִּים‎, see II. חת‎); — terror, caused by powerful cities, nations, kings, etc.: usually with suffix object Genitive 26:17 (of Tyre); elsewhere only Ezekiel 32: Ezekiel 26:27 (ᵑ6 ׳ח, גִּבּוֺרִים‎ Co ׳ח תם גבור‎), Ezekiel 26:30 (חִתִּיתָם‎, but read חַתִּים‎, see above); especially in phrase חַיִּים ח ׳נָתַן בארץ‎ cause one's terror (terror of oneself) in the land of the living Ezekiel 26:23; Ezekiel 26:24; Ezekiel 26:25 (strike out ᵐ5‎ Co), Ezekiel 26:26; Ezekiel 26:32. — חִתִּית‎ 16:3, 45 see חִתִּי‎ below חֵת‎ above.

חתך.def:
H2852. chathak

Niph`al Perfect עַלעַֿמְּךָ נֶחְתַּךְ שִׁבְעִים שָֽׁבֻעִים‎ Dan 9:24 seventy weeks are determined upon thy people.

H2853. chathal

Pu`al Perfect2feminine singular חֻתַּלְתְּ‎ and

Hoph`al Infinitive absolute הָחְתֵּל‎ be swathed, swaddled; — חֻתַּלְתְּ לֹא וְהָחְתֵּל הֻמְלַ֫חַתְּ לֹא וְהָמְלֵחַ‎ Ezek 16:4 and not at all wast thou rubbed with salt, and not at all wast thou swaddled, of Jerusalem under figure of infant.

חתלה.def:
H2854. chathullah

[חֲתֻלָּה‎] noun feminine swaddling-band (see BaNB 146) — only חֲתֻלֶּתוֺ וַעֲרָפֶל לְבֻשׁוֺ עָנָן בְּשׂוּמִי‎ Job 38:9 when I made cloud its garment, and thick darkness its swaddling-band, figurative of dark clouds enveloping the sea.

חתלן.def:
H2855. Chethlon

חֶתְלֹן‎ proper name, of a location, on the extreme northern boundary of Israel territory (in Ezekiel's conception), only ׳דֶּרֶךְ(ֿ)ח‎ Ezek 47:15; 48:1; modern „eitela nearly two hours from sea-coast, according to FurrerZPV viii, 27.

חתם.def:
H2856. chatham

חָתַם‎ verb seal, affix seal, seal up (Late Hebrew id.; Aramaic חֲתַם‎, ; Ethiopic Arabic (whence ) is loan-word according to Frä252) —

Qal Imperfect3masculine singular יַחְתֹּם‎ Job 9:7; 33:6, יַחְתּוֺם‎ 37:7, וַיַּחְתֹּם‎ Est 8:10, etc.; Imperative חֲתֹם‎ Dan 12:4, חֲתוֺם‎ Isa 8:16, חִתְמוּ‎ Est 8:8; Infinitive absolute חָתוֺם‎ Jer 32:44; construct לַחְתֹּם‎ Dan 9:24, + 9:24 Kt (Qr לְהָתֵם‎); Participle active חוֺתֵם‎ Ezek 28:12; pass. חָתוּם‎ Deut 32:24 2t., etc.; —

1 seal, affix one's seal, in attestation; seal with king's seal (בְּחֹתָמוֺ‎) 1Kin 21:8, המלך בְּטַבַּעַת‎ Est 8:8, 10; of covenant with ׳י‎, attested by seal (passive) Neh 10:1; 10:2; figurative, of ׳י‎ putting his seal upon (בְּ‎) discipline, i.e. ratifying it, Job 33:16; perhaps also upon hand of man (that man may know ׳י‎s ways) 37:7 see De; Di below

2 seal up hand of man, so that he cannot work with it (in winter).

2 seal up, fasten up by sealing, a deed of sale Jer 32:10-11,(opposed to הַגָּלוּי‎ that which was left open,), 32:14; 32:44, a book of prophecy Dan 12:4 (|| הַדְּבָרים סְתֹם‎), compare 12:9 (|| id.), 9:24 b; so in simileof unintelligible prophecy Isa 29:11 (twice in verse); בְּלְמֻּדָ֑י תּוֺרָה חֲתֹם‎ 8:16 seal up the teaching among my disciples, i.e. keep it securely (|| צוֺר‎); of ׳י‎s remembrance of offences בְּאוֺצְרֹתָ֑י חָתוּם‎ Deut 32:34 (|| עְמָּדִי כָּמֻס‎), so מִּשְׁעִי בִּצְרוֺר חָתוּם‎ Job 14:17 (|| עַלעֲֿוֺנִי וַתִּטְמֹּל‎); חָתוּם מַעְיָן‎ Song 4:12 a fountain sealed up, metaphor of chaste woman (|| נָעוּל (גַּל) גַּן‎); יַח כּוֺכָבִים ׳וּבְעַד‎ Job 9:7 and about the stars he putteth a seal (|| of forbidding sun to rise). — תָּכְנִית חוֺתֵם אַתָּה‎ Ezek 28:12 is obscure: thou wast one sealing proportion, i.e. perfection, — wast complete perfection, Ges Sm.; wast a sealer of symmetry see Da; wast a seal (ring) — i.e. חוֺתַם‎ construct — of proportion Manuscripts ᵑ9 ᵐ5‎ Hi compare Ew; text perhaps corrupt, see suggestions in Co. — Dan 9:24 a read Qr לְהָתֵם‎ (see תמם‎). Job 33:16; 37:7 see below

NöZMG 1886, 187; otherwise DlPr 91 LagBN 116) — construct חֹתֵן‎ Exod 18:1 + 9t., חֹתֶנְךָ‎ 18:6, חֹתְנוֺ‎ 3:1+ 9 t.; — usually of Moses' wife's father 3:1; 4:18; 18:1-2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 (twice in verse); 18:14; 18:15; 18:17; 18:24; 18:27 (all E), Num 10:29 (J), Judg 1:16; 4:11; of a Levite 19:4, 7, 9.

Hithpa`el make oneself a daughter's husband (Late Hebrew Hithpa`el id., Aramaic Ithpa`al id.) — Perfect2masculine plural וְהִתְחַתַּנְתֶּם‎ consecutive Josh 23:12; Imperfect וַיִּתְחַתֵּן‎ 1Kin 3:1; 2Chr 18:1-2; masculine תִּתְחַתֵּן‎ Deut 7:3; 1Sam 18:21; Imperative הִתְחַתֵּן‎ 18:22, הִתְחַתְּנוּ‎ Gen 34:9; Infinitive הִתְחַתֵּן‎ 1Sam 18:23 3t.; —

Qal Perfect ׳ח‎ Job 24:16, חָתַרְתִּי‎ Ezek 12:7; Imperfect וָאֶחְתֹּר‎ 8:8, יַחְתְּרוּ‎ 12:12; Amos 9:2, וַיַּחְתְּרוּ‎ Jonah 1:13; Imperative חֲתָרֿ‎ Ezek 8:8; 12:5; —
